initializes two actor records from the tables at `0x2dbf8` and `0x2eb24`, then
starts an asynchronous palette task. The following controller states submit
text tasks for event IDs `0x3e` and `0x3f` with styles `0x1615` and `0x1611`,
wait 10 and 30 ticks after their task flags clear, then start a 128-tick actor
transition; state 8 advances the main controller back to gameplay while that
transition continues. The
story catalog now validates these controller and text-task byte ranges,
extracts `A GREAT MAGICIAN.` and `A BRAVE WARRIOR.`, and maps their Scroll 1
destinations to cells `(4,22)` and `(12,26)`. The native controller now shows
those texts after message `0x41` and runs the 128-tick transition before
returning player control. Their layer-map writes are represented in the
native viewport as persistent blank regions, and each source clear immediately
rebuilds the visible planes so an unchanged camera position cannot leave stale
tiles onscreen. The stage catalog validates the
actor setup calls at `0x8f0e`, the move call at `0x8ffa`, both clear helpers,
and the selector table at `0x54f2`; generated origin and offset arrays feed
the runtime overlay. Helpers `0x548c` and `0x5532` use selectors 5 and 9 to
copy the corresponding actor-grid regions;
the native code records the corresponding 256-by-256-pixel regions and draws
Scroll 2 code zero / Scroll 3 transparent cells when rebuilding the viewport.
This covers the initial actor origins `(0,0x300)` and `(0x400,0x200)`, plus the
later first-actor origin `(0x200,0x300)`. The Scroll 1 to Window placement
remains an inferred screen transform, and the map overlay has not yet been
compared against rendered arcade output.
The native loop now applies the source palette brightness nibble to the four
Genesis palette slots during this transition. It follows the CPS task's
per-group word-zero gate and four-word update, steps down to the source's
minimum one-third intensity, then steps back up, queuing the return fade if
the down fade is still active. Source words are retained by the palette
catalog. Runtime setup at `0x7e6` ORs `0xf000` into every palette word; the
generator validates that instruction and converts the initial palette at
full brightness. The native fade then reproduces the fifteen three-tick
brightness steps and the final three-tick completion pass before returning
the palette to full brightness. Genesis's three-bit channels still quantize
the fade, and the task's group-mask accumulator is not modeled independently.
Rendered timing/color comparison remains pending.
The following actor transition is now cataloged directly from source: behavior
8 selects ten seven-frame loops from table `0x15666`; the source actor creator
at `0x9034` starts mode 0 at `(728,904)`, then the behavior handler chains
additional modes through the queue allocator. The animation catalog validates
the table bytes, animation initializer, behavior-8 setup, and actor creator,
and emits per-mode uncompressed tile codes, raw descriptors, CPS-template
resolved origins, and 8/16-tick frame holds into `build/willow_walk.h`. Native
code now chains all ten actors, applies their validated 8.8 movement vector
and mode-specific delays, streams their uncompressed frames, and draws them
within Genesis sprite limits during the 128-tick window. The stage sprite pack
carries all 32,768 CPS graphics codes uncompressed, including this actor's
frame range, so no runtime decompression or arcade code is required. Native chained
actor timing and first-origin composition are now modeled. Animation frame
validation uses the full `0x0000`–`0x7fff` CPS graphics code range. The broader
code-range check is separate from the offline whole-ROM scan's conservative
`0x5000` candidate filter, which helps reject program bytes that resemble
animation records. Each actor frame is
repacked into a 64-pattern native atlas slot, with each 2x2 CPS tile group
drawn as one Genesis sprite. This keeps the ten-actor sequence within the
Genesis sprite list (at most 28 entries for these source descriptors) and
reserves patterns after the Stage 0 background/actor caches, before the timer
glyphs. Exact palette task completion timing, both actor-map changes, CPS
clipping/order, and rendered comparison against the arcade remain pending.
Both story destinations are source Scroll 1 cells; the native Window renderer
subtracts five columns to fit the 320-pixel viewport. This uses the same
source-to-native offset as the timer's `(40,3)/(43,3)` to `(35,1)/(38,1)`
mapping, so it remains a viewport-layout inference pending rendered comparison.
The native text writer also advances at the source parser's fixed 40
characters per row, including mid-word row breaks, instead of reflowing by
word.
The opening task's 29-tick controller timer is not the message lifetime:
parser state 0 clears its task flags at the `/` terminator but leaves its
Scroll 1 glyph cells written. The native HUD keeps that text after task
completion and clears only the four timer cells when first showing the timer,
instead of clearing the entire Window plane.
Story text now enables the full Genesis Window plane so those source row
coordinates remain visible. The runtime keeps that full-screen mode active
while persistent story text is present; the timer can update its four cells
without reducing the Window to two rows and hiding text below row 1. When no
story text is active, the timer-only view keeps its two-row Window.
It does not yet send system command `0xf4`, reproduce the controller-state
command verbatim; its Z80 handler resets sequencer/YM state, which the native
loop approximates with `XGM_stopPlay()` while preserving active PCM voices.
The early-exit writer at `0xcf6a` clears a task record, sets `a5+0x03c2`, and
frees asynchronous task slot `0x00c0` through `TRAP #2`. Before freeing it, the
writer calls `0xc230`, which merges a four-color row from the source table at
`0x0e5080` into CPS palette RAM at `0x91c000` (offset selected by task byte
`+0x20`). The task's entry and trigger are still unresolved, so the native
loop does not guess which event should set the phase gate. The controller-state
exit writes remain unported, and the display placement and task lifetime still
need runtime comparison before treating this sequence as arcade-accurate.
The timer gate itself skips updates when word `a5+0x03d2` is nonzero, either
byte `a5+0x03e9` or `a5+0x03cf` is nonzero, or byte `a5+0x03e2` is at least 2.
The `a5+0x03d2` word is a global actor freeze: the per-frame state manager
sets it during its special mode, clears it on completion, and the shared actor
dispatcher skips actor state handling while it is set. Its manager counter
advances by two per update and releases the freeze at `0x0100`, for 128 updates.
The triggering task state at `0xf4f0` queues sound command `0x23` and writes
`0xff` to the manager trigger byte; the native prototype has no verified event
or sound mapping for this source transition yet.
Below 16 seconds it can also defer a tick to queue a cue. Later callers at
`0x9552` and `0x9618` call the same gate under their own state checks. At
`0x4eda`, the subcounter reloads 59 on borrow and decrements the seconds/minutes
as BCD. The display writer at
`0x4f18` writes the two digit groups at Scroll 1 addresses `0x91140c` and
`0x91158c`. The Stage 0 setup selects Scroll 1 base `0x910000` and X scroll
`0xffc0`; applying MAME's Scroll 1 `tilemap0_scan` layout maps the writes to
map cells `(40,3)` and `(43,3)`. The catalog validates the base and scroll
setup, both writer addresses, and the resulting cells. The native HUD now
streams the two alternating Scroll 1 digit layouts from an uncompressed
640-byte glyph asset, updates the minute/second digits from the BCD timer, and
shows the compact display at the top-right of the 320-pixel Genesis viewport.
It places the minute pair at columns 35–36 and the seconds pair at columns
38–39, fitting the full timer into the rightmost four cells of the Genesis
40-column plane. This is a native re-layout of the source map cells (40,3) and
(43,3); exact arcade-to-Genesis horizontal parity remains unverified. Since
Genesis already assigns all four CRAM palettes to the
actors and background, the glyph pixels map to the closest active background
palette; text colors therefore remain an approximation. This screen placement
has not yet been compared against rendered arcade frames. The native runtime
now advances the timer and phase countdown while the opening task runs. It
pauses the timer during the phase message and post-phase actor transition, then
resumes it when the controller returns to ordinary play; the exhausted
900-tick phase countdown no longer leaves the gameplay timer frozen. The
source gate's other asynchronous-task and global-freeze conditions remain
unmodeled, so those pause cases are not exact. See the
[MAME Scroll 1 mapper](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1_v.cpp#L2201-L2205).
The per-stage event
pointer table at `0xa8ea` contains six four-byte records: `27 00 00 00`,
`2e 2d 00 00`, `41 40 2f 00`, `45 44 00 00`, `46 00 00 00`, and
`48 00 00 00`. They resolve to post-stage story messages, including the
forest spirit's identity and Elora's mission, the Galladoorn defeat, the
endgame warning, and Bavmorda's final threat. The initializer feeds each
selected message ID through the shared asynchronous task dispatcher at
`0x15cc`. Catalog validation checks the controller targets, state-8
instructions, six countdown indices, message record lookup, delimiters, and
text tile writer. The catalog exports both the source table rows and the
reverse-index display sequences with their corresponding message text. Native story-screen
timing and presentation still need porting before wiring native stage
progression. State 5
queues work word `0x0c00` with parameters 3 and 6 through `0x1f14`; these are
separate from audio words queued through `0x783c`. State 7 also queues its own
sound words through `0x785e`/`0x786a`. This chain advances from controller
state and task completion, not a player-position boundary. The catalog now
traces the task queue beyond the command IDs: task `0x0c00` selects
handler `0x582c`; substate zero at `0x5858` queues task `0x1000` with the same
completion parameter, waits for `a5+0x02c0`, clears CPS video memories, posts
completion parameter plus four, and clears the stage lock `a5+0x7891`. Task
`0x1000` selects handler `0x509c`; substate zero at `0x50c6` runs the palette
transition routine across six CPS palette ranges and releases `a5+0x02c0` when
its accumulated source threshold reaches `0x1fa`. Its step at `0x5260` checks
each indexed palette group. If its first word has nonzero brightness, it
subtracts `0x1000` from four consecutive words; otherwise it marks that group
in a status mask. The routine sums those masks before signaling completion.
MAME's CPS-1 palette conversion says a zero brightness nibble leaves colors at
one-third intensity, so the arcade reaches minimum brightness before clearing
the old display memory, rather than fading to black ([palette builder](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1_v.cpp)).
The task handler bytes and both dispatch paths are checked by the stage
catalog. Native stage transition code must reproduce the palette transition,
clear, and completion ordering with Genesis hardware and native 68000 code.
When the timed event sequence ends, controller state 1 branches to a dedicated
`0x0bc4` dispatcher. It visits 16 records at 64-byte strides, tests each
record's active byte, and dispatches its behavior byte through eight handlers
at `0x0bea`. This actor route is now byte-checked separately; it does not
provide a player spawn coordinate.
The transition then advances the stage counter: values 0–4
advance, stage 5 stays at 5, and unexpected values above 5 reset to 0 after
incrementing. It calls stage setup routines `0x2e1c`, `0x2d80`, `0x2f8a`, and
`0x381bc`, then clears state/timer fields before resuming at `0x978`. Grid 6
contains no chunks; grid 7 contains 12 nonempty selectors.
Neither grid is reached by this normal route, so their entry paths still need
to be traced. The stage catalog now extracts the six rows loaded by `0x2d80`
and `0x2f8a` into `stage_transition.stage_setup_parameters`: stage-indexed
words written to `a5+0x038e`, `+0x0390`, `+0x0392`, `+0x0370`, and `+0x0372`.
These configuration values are byte-validated, but they do not establish
later-stage player spawn positions, so the native transition still needs those
initializer paths before it can reposition Willow accurately. Its final call
to `0x381bc` adjusts the stage-indexed `a5+0x0346` counter using the byte table
at `0x3819a` and field `a5+0x0291`; those instructions do not write Willow's
position fields. The stage catalog now checks this routine and exports its
six reachable table values separately from the position data.
The catalog also validates a separate descriptor-based actor state-4 handler at
`0x2d89a` (distinct from the stage-setup routine at `0x2d80`). It indexes a
12-entry selector table with object `+33`; its entry also advances substate,
sends sound command `0x10fb` through `0x786a`, then calls `0x1e88`, which
sets task lock `a5+0x7891`, queues asynchronous task `0x0c00` with parameter
3 through `0x1f14`, and waits via `0x1750` before reading six words into shared
controller target, camera-parameter, and player-position fields. Controller
state 5 calls this same helper for the same task and parameter. Other flows use
the helper too, so this confirms shared task behavior but not a proven actor
creation path into normal stage progression. The first six
coordinate pairs are `(1616,64)`, `(64,2472)`, `(1616,64)`, `(848,64)`,
`(1616,64)`, and `(64,2472)`. The fixed batch at `0x2d55e` does not directly
dispatch to that handler: its class-4 records store word `0x0106` at `+32`, and the ordinary
50-record dispatcher at `0xffa2` reads byte `+32` (`1`) and routes it to
`0x115ee`. That dispatch does not use the separate `0x2d7d0` substate table;
the batch's `+33` byte is `6`, which is outside the four leading selector
offsets at `0x115fc`. Applying the dispatcher math reads the word `0x323b` from
the handler body and computes odd target `0x14837`, invalid for a 68000
instruction fetch. The fixed batch therefore does not establish a valid route
to the coordinate handler or prove a normal Stage 1 actor path. The coordinate
handler's creator and dispatch path still have no proven link to normal
stage progression. The catalog tests candidate positions against the vertically
flipped selector grids: `actor+33` values 1, 5, and 6 land in blank cells across
all grids; value 7 lands in populated cells only for stages 3 and 5; value 11
only for stage 5. This narrows possible uses but does not assign the handler to
a stage, so its coordinates remain candidates and are not used as native
spawns. The catalog exports both dispatch paths with source-byte checks while
its actual creator is traced.
The stage initializer at `0xa0e0` is now byte-checked as three separate
routes. Its ordinary stage-counter-zero path requires
`a5+0x0348 == 0` and `a5+0x0344 == 0`, calls `0x2dfe`, then writes `(192,512)`
to the player world coordinates at `a5+0x0408/+0x040c` and `(192,512)` to the
companion coordinates at `a5+0x0488/+0x048c`. A separate branch is entered
only when the stage counter is 3 and `a5+0x03a0` is clear; it sets that flag, resets controller
state/timer fields, calls `0x2dfe`, and writes `0x1050` to `a5+0x8fb2`,
`(192,4096)` to `a5+0x0408/+0x040c`, and `(192,4096)` to
`a5+0x0488/+0x048c`, before initializing additional object records. This
special branch is preserved as source evidence, not treated as the spawn for
every later stage. The remaining stage-counter path only sets `a5+0x0348`,
advances controller state, clears timers, and returns without writing player
coordinates. A linear main-CPU disassembly cross-reference finds direct writes
to player globals `a5+0x0408/+0x040c` in the Stage 0 and special Stage 3
branches, plus the separate descriptor handler at `0x2d89a`; that handler’s
creator is not linked to normal progression. This narrows the next trace to
finding who creates its actor and which selector it receives. The stage catalog
validates all three initializer paths; later-stage spawn coordinates remain
unproven, so native progression cannot yet place Willow accurately.
Controller state 7 separately indexes a six-entry actor-position table at
`0xac46`: `(0,256)`, `(0,0)`, `(1024,256)`, `(1536,256)`, `(2560,256)`, and
`(2048,256)`. It copies each pair to a sequence actor's `+6/+10` fields and
copies their low ten bits to shared fields `a5+0x32/+0x34`. The catalog
validates these bytes; this is sequence-actor placement, not evidence for
Willow's later-stage spawn coordinates.
The Stage 0 controller allocates animated tile tasks from a 16-record pool at
`a5+0x7042`; the byte-checked setup at `0x830c` points two tasks at data
`0xea660` and `0xea700`. It then allocates a separate linked child at
`(1216,64)`. The child is queue-class-8 behavior 8: the class-8 dispatcher
routes it to `0xfadc`, whose state-0 setup queues sound command `0x25`, loads a
62-tick state-2 timer, sets interaction bounds, and installs animation data at
`0xf4d0`. State 2 calls visibility each update, advances to state 4 at timeout,
and dispatches shared event-list callbacks `0x709c`/`0x70ae` on alternating
global frames. Timer expiry enters state 4; the next scheduler update frees the
record through `0x2b20`. The stage catalog now byte-checks the selector-8
dispatch, state-0/state-2 handlers, and release. The interrupted event-scan
trace has now been corrected and completed: the caller's nonzero behavior
byte selects the 32-byte map at `0x7102`, so behavior 8 does **not** use the
zero-behavior map at `0x7122`. Its map rejects candidate behaviors 8, 21, and
22, routes behavior 10 to `0x71ee`, and routes the other table entries
(including behaviors 1 and 9) to `0x7152`. Candidates must have byte `+0=1`.
The catalog byte-checks the full scan, both maps, callback offsets, and the
three overlap handlers, and exports all 32 behavior-8 callback destinations.
The default overlap callback sets candidate `+0=2`, `+2=4`, and clears
`+3/+4`; behavior 10's callback sets `+0=2`, `+2=6`. Either successful overlap
ends the scan. Both use unsigned 16-bit bounds comparisons with equality
accepted. The linked-flag callback at `0x719a` belongs to candidate behavior 8
under the **zero-behavior caller** map, not behavior 9 under this actor's map.
These filters alone do not prove which actors populate the shared event
lists. This actor's callbacks, lifecycle, and render path remain absent from
the native runtime. For stage counter 1, state 7
creates two more tile tasks at
`0xa848`, pointing to `0xea120` and `0xea1c0`. Their parameters select graphics
bank 2, destination tile indices 4 and 5, and 8-tick frame holds. The byte-
validated dispatcher at `0x0bc4` routes these descriptors to handler `0x0c0a`;
its state-0 setup computes CGC destinations `0x91c880` and `0x91c8a0`, and its
state-2 updater copies each next 32-byte 8x8 tile frame. The catalog exports
all five source frames per task. These records animate graphics memory and are
not screen actors or Willow position data.

A separate 8-record actor pool at `a5+0x7490` dispatches through `0x26da6`.
Its behavior-0 handlers at `0x26de8`, `0x26dfc`, and `0x26e82` select streams
`0x27222` and `0x27318` and can create child actors. Their pool bases and dispatcher code show they are separate systems. Their
exact connection to Stage 1 remains unproven, so the catalog keeps them
separate from the tile tasks. Native runtime support for the two
Stage 1 CGC tile animations and stage transition integration remain open.
The runtime draws both background layers through the active stage's selector
grid. `setActiveStage` resets the stage graphics cache and stage-indexed
viewport, palette, and collision lookups use its selection, but its only current
call selects stage 0 at startup. The source transition controller still does
not call the native stage setup, so later stages are not reachable in play.
The renderer flips selector-grid rows vertically: Stage 1's occupied rows 14–15
map to world Y `0..512`, and its generic camera bounds are X `0..3776`, Y
`0..288`. Carrying the current Stage 0 spawn `(192,512)` into Stage 1 would
clamp the camera to Y `288` and put Willow at screen Y `224`; that is not a
verified Stage 1 entry. The Stage 1 camera parameters `(192,80)` do not by
themselves identify a player spawn, so transition setup remains disabled until
its actor-entry path is tied to the normal route.
The camera rebuilds its viewport in 16-pixel map-cell steps and applies VDP
plane scroll offsets between those boundaries. Scroll 3
tiles are split into 8x8 Genesis patterns and share a bounded
cache with Scroll 2. The runtime retains cached source patterns between camera
steps and reloads the viewport after cache exhaustion. Scroll 2/3 priority now
follows the source control value. Player collision probes now resolve their
property attributes from the selected stage's Scroll 2 chunk at the same
world coordinates used by movement. The separate Scroll 1 gameplay layer and
the source camera's absolute map-to-screen offset remain unresolved.
Scroll 3 graphics are decoded from the physical 4 MiB region, which contains
32x32 source tiles through `0x1fff`. Stage 7 chunk 6 contains map code `0x2004`;
after the game's `0x0a00` base this requests tile `0x2a04`, beyond the available
graphics data, so the native renderer correctly leaves that cell transparent.

`tools/cps1_stage_preview.py` composes the selected stage's nonempty chunks
with its stage-indexed source palettes, for example
`python3 tools/cps1_stage_preview.py 0 scroll2 --output build/stage0.ppm`.
This verifies the ROM selector-to-chunk assignments and source graphics as a
single stage map. The Genesis runtime streams the active Scroll 2 and Scroll 3
viewports as the camera moves. The full reference image remains offline, and
CPS Scroll 2/3 priority follows the source control register; Scroll 1 is not
yet composed by the gameplay renderer.

`make collision-catalog` decodes the 46 eight-byte terrain property records
referenced by the movement collision routines and the twelve four-word probe
profiles used by `0x3b0a`. The JSON retains the offline records; a generated
header links flags, shape bytes, both facing X-threshold bytes, the player
ground/ascent offsets, and all twelve `0x3b66` movement probes into the native
ROM; it also emits all four signed 8.8 vectors from `0x136b0`. The native jump
launch and ascent checks read their `0x3a74` and `0x3b02`
probe coordinates from those generated records. Normal movement now uses the
Stage 0 profile-3 center probe from entry 3 of `0x3b66` with the source
`0x40a0` solid-surface correction, then runs the moved-X `0x38f6` side checks.
This removes the earlier `0x39fe` lower-body test that incorrectly blocked
ordinary steps. Left/right walking applies the selected vector's Y component
before collision checks. The native movement accumulator now keeps a full
16-bit fractional word, matching the source's 8.8-to-16.16 vector conversion;
the actor world-position and collision path still projects to whole pixels.
Full joystick-to-vector selection and full 16.16 collision integration remain
unmodeled. The source
property lookup uses `((cell_attribute & 0xfc) << 1)` to index an eight-byte
record at `0x4712`. Scroll 2's high attribute byte supplies that class. The
Stage 0's player actor is initialized with byte `+32 = 3`, selecting the
nonzero profile tables. Its lower-body pair from `0x39fe` is
`(-10,+24),(+10,+24)`; both points call the one-way surface helper `0x3f62`
and apply its fractional-Y correction during the jump-launch path. Normal
movement uses the profile-3 center probe from `0x3b0a`, followed by the
profile-3 facing-side points from
`0x38f6` at `(+12,-24),(-12,-24)` when facing right and the reversed order
when facing left, using the `0x3e4c` solid-shape correction. The side
collision flag does not cancel horizontal movement in the source caller. The
preceding `0x4190` probe uses the first facing-specific profile-3 point and
sets object byte `+31`; a hit sends normal movement into state 4. State 4 runs
two four-tick substates, selects `0x1315c` and then `0x13160`, and increments
the main state to 6 when its timer ends at `0x128e2`. The native path now
pauses movement and action input during those eight ticks and renders the
facing-specific entry poses from both tables. Their first records last 20 and
8 ticks respectively, longer than each four-tick substate. State 6 selects
`0x13164` for a 48-tick entry sequence; its six source frames and per-frame
horizontal origins are now generated and rendered. The native frame timer now
waits until the update after `0x1f30` selects that table before beginning the
first duration, matching the source's `0x1f4c` call on substate 2. After its
48-tick entry,
source state 6 calls `0x20d2` to calculate a direction toward the global
coordinates at `a5+0x184c/+0x1850`, stores a 16-way target heading in object
byte `+49`, and advances its current heading one step every eight ticks. The
native path now translates the source's ratio-based octant classifier and
step cadence, initializes the heading to 4 or 12 from the actor's X position
as the source does, and recomputes the aim from the live translated shared
target coordinates at every timer expiry (rather than fixed coordinates).
It renders the `0x1316c` transition pose during each turn,
then renders the `0x1318c` settled pose for 16 ticks. The next state 6
substate holds that pose for 16 ticks and calls `0x3b0a` once; a contact
selects the seven-tick `0x13160` pose, otherwise the player waits 40 ticks
before checking the shared `0x1d8e` LFSR against the Stage 0 mask `0x1111`
from `0x12a96`. The source shifts the low byte of `a5+0x0346` right three,
masks to an even byte offset, then indexes the word table; this selects row
`(counter >> 4) & 15`. `a5+0x0346` is initialized from the player-two option
lookup (`0x30` with no P2 buttons held) and advances once per active frame,
saturating at `0xffff`. Its low byte selects rows 0–15 as the counter advances;
after saturation it remains at row 15. Native recovery explicitly narrows to
that low byte before selecting the row. The animation catalog byte-checks the
lookup at `0x12a64` and exports its row formula. Failed checks retry one tick
later.
The object catalog byte-validates the `0x20d2` heading classifier, its eight
octant bases at `0x2144`, and its 32-step divider at `0x214c`, and records
these source inputs in `build/willow_objects.json`. The animation catalog also
checks the base table and now generates the values consumed by the native
heading calculation in `build/willow_walk.h`.
The normal Stage 0 initializer does not write the shared target at
`a5+0x184c/+0x1850`; startup clears both words, so its initial target is
`(0,0)`. The explicit X=448 write at `0xa186` belongs to the separate
stage-counter-3 branch. The later `0xa57e` Y adjustment has no established
normal Stage 0 caller. The object catalog validates these writes and their
branch context.
The two facing entries in both `0x1316c` and `0x1318c` are identical. Their
frames are 4x4 CPS blocks with horizontal origin 6 (`0x0e88` followed by
`0x0fc0` for the turn; `0x0fc0` for settled facing). The records are
validated and emitted into `build/willow_walk.h` from the offline catalog.
The player state dispatch table at `0x1276e` maps state 6 to handler
`0x128ec` and state 8 to `0x12ac6`. A successful mask check at `0x12a8a`
sets state 6 and substate 0, so state 6 restarts its `0x13164` 48-tick entry
sequence; it does not return control or proceed directly to state 8. The
native path now preserves the preceding pose for the state transition tick,
then starts that entry sequence on the next handler tick, both on first entry
and after a successful mask check. When state 6 exits through substate 12,
the source clears to state 0; its next handler update enters normal state 2,
selects `0x13154`, and sets facing from the player's X relative to the moving
Stage 0 target, initially zero in arcade coordinates (native x=32 after the
camera translation). The native loop now models that one-tick entry at startup
and after state 6 exits. State 6's later transitions and state 8 movement
substates remain incomplete.
Remaining records in the state 4
tables, precise per-record animation origins, and other player
probe profiles, exact slope
response, landing state transitions, and collision-to-sprite-anchor alignment
remain unfinished.
The `0x3e28` map helper's byte offset is recorded as
`((x & 0x03f0) << 2) + (((~y) & 0x0300) << 4) + (((~y) & 0x00f0) >> 2)`;
it addresses a vertically inverted 64x64-cell map ring, with the attribute byte
at offset 2 in each cell. The default profile is now sampled in stage world
coordinates. Correcting the remaining source object-anchor offsets, reproducing
all probe profiles and collision responses, and matching landing states remain
unfinished.

The background tile exporters follow Willow's `WL24B` mapper and MAME's CPS
tile layouts. Scroll 1 emits both 8x8 source halves because the tilemap index
selects the layout; Scroll 2 maps logical codes `0x0000-0x1fff` to decoded
16x16 tile codes `0x4000-0x5fff`; Scroll 3 maps codes `0x0a00-0x1fff` to 32x32
source tiles. Startup code initializes tilemap pages at `0x910000`, `0x914000`,
and `0x918000`, then fills them with default Scroll 1, Scroll 3, and Scroll 2
tiles. `make scroll1-map-catalog` decodes the table at `0x5c7e` according to
the writer at `0x5b20`, preserving tile-code and fill modes, CPS palette and
flip attributes, and split 64x64 tilemap coordinates. Map `0x0d` is selected in
codes mode at `0x565e` from routine `0x5630`, called by `0x3807c` when `a5+0x28f`
is nonzero and bit 5 of `a5+0x68` is set. These flags come from the inverted
CPS DSWC byte: bit 7 selects Test mode and bit 5 enables “Display Debug Infos”
in Willow's [MAME input definitions](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1.cpp).
Map `0x0d` is therefore a test-mode debug-info overlay, not ordinary gameplay
art. The exact displayed values and palette mapping remain unresolved, so it
is not yet composited into the native scene. Map catalogs also document viewer
chunks, and the stage-selector table is
separately cataloged. Native Scroll 2 and Scroll 3 stage scrolling rebuild the
visible tile cache at map-cell boundaries; exact runtime layer priority remains
to be implemented.

The codes-mode parser now follows `0x5b20` byte-for-byte: each segment has one
attribute byte followed by its glyph-code run. This fixes earlier output that
mistook neighboring glyphs for tile attributes. The uncalled candidate streams
0–9 decode to `CREDIT`, `INSERT COIN`, `GAME OVER`, the multi-line warning,
`CONTINUE`, `RANKING`, `PRESS START BUTTON`, `1 PLAYER ONLY`, `1 OR 2 PLAYERS`,
and `FREE PLAY`. Their source cells and line breaks are recorded in
`build/willow_scroll1_maps.json`. The native prompt scene uses map `0x06`;
runtime routes for the other system/menu maps have not been verified yet.

The selector scan also finds Scroll 1 maps `0x0a` (fill mode) and `0x0b` (codes
mode) at `0x8b36` and `0x8b46`. Between them the routine calls `0x8c6e` and
`0x8bf2` to write additional tile data. The code at `0x8b26`
returns at `0x8b24` unless bit 0 of `a5+0x02af` is set; on the set path it
increments word `a5+0x0008` by 2 before loading either map. The map catalog
validates this guard, the increment, call order, and helper bytes against the
ROM. The caller is now identified as state 13 in the dispatcher at `0x8882`:
its word-offset table entry at `0x88a8` resolves to `0x8b26`; adjacent entries
select `0x8af6` and `0x8b70` for states 12 and 14. This places the map writes in
that state's transition sequence, but does not prove the state runs in ordinary
Stage 0 play or establish what sets the `a5+0x02af` gate. `0x8c6e` fills ten
rows in four map columns with code `0x7020`; `0x8bf2`
writes six vertically advancing tile-code runs to those columns using the
writer at `0x8c5a`. The parent that sets this flag and the maps' gameplay role
remain unresolved, so these maps must not be assumed to be the ordinary
gameplay HUD. Map `0x0f` is selected at `0xba1e` after routine `0xb9e0`
initializes a Scroll 1 tilemap region. The `0x0f` call is inside state handler
`0xb9e0`: it writes two columns of 18 Scroll 1 character codes from the
`0xbac8` table (`A` through `Z`, followed by punctuation), overlays map `0x0f`,
and installs a variable marker tile before entering `0xbe60`. The following
state setup at `0xba54` initializes cursor coordinates and the input handler at
`0xbb52` moves the selection over the grid. This is a character-entry UI (most
likely a high-score name entry screen); its path from gameplay and exact
surrounding screen have not yet been established. It should be implemented as
a native UI state when the native game reaches the matching flow, not drawn as
a gameplay layer. The `0x0a`/`0x0b` pair is also not a persistent gameplay
foreground: state handler `0x8b26` first checks bit 0 of `a5+0x2af`, advances
its state, then draws map `0x0a`, clears and templates the Scroll 1 area, draws
map `0x0b`, and emits three text strings through `0x1e54`. The caller dispatches
state offsets from `a5+8` at `0x8882`; the exact screen flow and bit writer are
still unresolved, so this pair should remain a candidate transient overlay
rather than being inserted into the Stage 0 renderer.

The helper at `0x425a6` is a distinct Scroll 1 writer. It toggles object byte
`+76`; on the active path it selects a 16x16 block from the current Scroll 2
map using object word `+74`, extracts each cell's two-bit palette group, and
writes Scroll 1 codes `0x7000`–`0x7003` with zero attributes. The inactive path
branches to `0x41668`, which restores the default Scroll 1 and Scroll 3
tilemaps. Input branch `0x424cc` reaches the helper when bit 0 is newly pressed;
adjacent input branches alter the selected map and its Scroll 2/3 view. The
dispatch path is now identified: sampler `0x1a80` inverts DSWC at `0x80001e`
and stores bit 7 in `a5+0x28f`; dispatcher `0x80a6` uses that flag to select
entry `0x45a8c`, which initializes the mode and transfers to `0x415c2`. MAME's
Willow DIP definition identifies DSWC bit 7 as Test mode. The catalog
byte-validates the sampler, mode branch, entry, and overlay handler. This is a
Test-mode diagnostic/map-inspection UI, not an ordinary Stage 0 actor. If the
native port reproduces service/Test mode, implement it as a separate native UI
state; do not add its palette overlay to the persistent stage renderer.

The main-CPU image also contains HUD-looking text records beginning at
`0x5f6a`: `1UP`, `HI`, `2UP`, `VITAL`, `P=`, `GOLD`, and `TIME`, each preceded
by three layout bytes. The text routines at `0x7b1a`/`0x7b34` turn character
bytes into Scroll 1 codes by adding `0x7000` or `0x7100`; the renderer at
`0x7994` selects a Scroll 1 destination and palette state before writing glyphs.
This establishes recoverable character graphics and candidate HUD labels, but
the record coordinates, palette meanings, gameplay call path, and dynamic
health/gold/time value sources still need to be traced together before those
labels can be placed accurately in the native Stage 0 scene.
`make hud-catalog` now byte-validates these seven candidate records and emits
their raw coordinates/style bytes and both source glyph-code variants to
`build/willow_hud_candidates.json`; it deliberately does not treat them as a
confirmed gameplay HUD.
The renderer's verified `BSR.W 0x7994` call sites include `0x7912`, `0x7ada`,
`0x7db8`, `0x7ed2`, and `0x7f96`. They establish several generic text-render
paths, but do not identify a caller that selects the `0x5f6a` records, so the
candidate labels still lack a proven Stage 0 placement path.
An offline 68000 disassembly confirms that the Stage 0 task setup at `0xa264`
submits callback `0x78f0` with parameters `0x2e` and `0x1302`; callback state
zero dispatches to the text routine at `0x7912`, which calls `0x7994` to
derive its ROM text and Scroll 1 destination pointers from the task context.
The parser clears its asynchronous task flags at the `/` terminator. The
other listed entries are render helpers or a static “SELECT PLAYERS” screen,
not evidence that the `0x5f6a` labels are drawn during gameplay. The HUD
record addresses also have no direct PC-relative `LEA` references in the
assembled main-CPU image. The exact mapping from callback parameters through
`0x7994` to text records still needs verification; this scan does not rule out
indexed or computed references and does not prove the HUD records are unused.
The scheduler boundary is partially resolved: `TRAP #0` at `0x15cc` vectors to
`0x15d0`, which stores the callback, `D1`, and `D2` into the selected work-RAM
task slot. Callback `0x78f0` then obtains its working frame through the global
pointer at `a5-0x7dfc`; `0x7994` reads bytes at frame offsets `+17` and `+18`,
uses them to derive a text pointer in the ROM block beginning at `0x70000`, and
selects the Scroll 1 destination and palette. The parser at `0x7912` consumes
that string pointer. This does not establish a path from the candidate label
records at `0x5f6a` to the Stage 0 task; those labels still lack a proven
gameplay caller and value source.
`make hud-font-assets` extracts the uncompressed ASCII `0x20`–`0x5f` glyphs
for both Scroll 1 layouts and a separate full 256-glyph left-layout atlas for
source text. The font tool rotates each pixel index so CPS Scroll 1's
transparent pen 15 becomes Genesis pen 0 while source color pens 0–14 become
Genesis pens 1–15. The full atlas is included uncompressed in the ROM. Native
story text packs its used source glyphs into VRAM tiles 1984–2047, preserving
stable glyph-to-tile assignments while multiple lines remain on screen. The
same renderer accepts byte-counted front-end records, including a zero byte
as a real glyph. The native prompt scene uses it for the source `PRESS START
BUTTON` string.

The native startup currently shows the source-backed `PRESS START BUTTON`
string from Scroll 1 map `0x06` at decoded cell `(17,15)`. The generated
`willow_frontend.h` is emitted with the map catalog and rejects changes to the
text, row, contiguous columns, or palette before the runtime uses it. Genesis
Start enters the native one-player Stage 0 prototype. This remains an interim
prompt scene: it clears gameplay planes and sprites and does not reproduce the
arcade title artwork, timed actor entrances, attract loop, or full menu. The
current Scroll 1 map catalog does not provide a verified runtime route for
that title screen: maps `0x0a/0x0b` belong to a guarded transient state, map `0x0d`
is a Test-mode debug overlay, and map `0x0f` belongs to character entry. Their
validated callers do not identify title or attract screen drawing. The stage
catalog now validates the ordinary pre-game state's first task as well as the
start edge. Main state dispatch at `0x80f2` initializes through `0x821e`, then
the scripted state at `0x823e` submits system task `0x1000` with style 3 through
`0x1e54`. Task type `0x10` selects callback `0x509c`; its state-zero handler
updates Scroll 1 map state until `a5+0x02c0` is set. State `0x8252` then
advances to `0x65a4`, which restores the default Scroll 1/2/3 tilemap pages.
The exact task content, destination, and complete attract/title composition
remain unresolved. The input handler at `0x8186` requires the `a5+0x02a4` gate.
Its writer at `0x1b12` sets that flag when `(a5+0x0066 & 0x3f) == 7` and
clears it otherwise; caller `0x1aa0` invokes the writer only when bit 7 of
`a5+0x0068` is set. Those fields are the sampled DSWC/DSWD switch bytes. The
input handler accepts newly pressed bits `0x10/0x20`, derives the player-count
byte from bit `0x20`, calls gameplay reset `0x0978`, queues callback `0x92d2`,
and transfers to `0x1636`. These gate checks are exported in `front_end_start`.
Thus the start edge and initial pre-game task are traced, while the full
front-end flow remains incomplete. These checks are exported in
`front_end_attract` and `front_end_start` in `build/willow_stage_maps.json`.
After that initial fade and map reset, main state 2 enters controller `0x8266`.
Its setup at `0x82a4` reloads palette data and initializes the display, then
`0x82be` creates an actor record at `a5+0x0402` using the data pointer
`0x2ea24` and schedules tasks `0x1012`, `0x1014`, and `0x1016`. After the
180-tick wait, state `0x83b0` initializes a second actor at `a5+0x0482` using
data pointer `0x2f24c`, schedules task `0x1018`, and starts a 60-tick wait.
Those task IDs select separate palette-group fade handlers in the shared
`0x509c` dispatcher: `0x1012` fades `0x91c000`–`0x91c3ff`, `0x1014` fades
`0x91c400`–`0x91c7ff`, `0x1016` fades `0x91c800`–`0x91cbff`, and `0x1018`
fades `0x91cc00`–`0x91cfff`. Each raises color brightness in `0x1000` steps
until its palette-group mask clears. The shared animation selector at `0x1f30`
reads actor byte `+15`, doubles it to index a big-endian relative-offset word,
then adds that offset to the actor data base. The attract catalog now validates
this selector and resolves four candidate table entries:
`0x2ea24[0x50/0x51]` points to `0x33a24/0x33b24`, and
`0x2f24c[0x68/0x69]` points to `0x3124c/0x3134c`. Their target bytes and
`+8` words are exported alongside record walks that use the shared `0x1f4c`
length and indirect-record rules. Candidate stream `0x33b24` contains codes
`0x4efb` and `0x542e`; `0x3124c` begins with code `0x6404`. The catalog also
derives candidate tile grids with the same CPS row stepping and horizontal
flip rule as the native sprite renderer: `0x4efb` is a flipped 1x2 block,
`0x542e` is 1x1, and `0x6404` is 5x1. These targets, walks, and tile grids are
recorded in `front_end_attract.attract_scene.candidate_indexed_actor_targets`.
This also confirms that the full graphics-code range matters for animation
extraction. Source tile previews remain inconclusive about whether these
entries belong to the title actors; their live `+15` values, state meanings,
and frame composition remain unresolved.
The story catalog also checks the pre-game controller's later text sequence at
`0x8480`: message `0x34` is submitted with style `0x1607` at Scroll 1 cell
`(6,14)`, then message `0x35` with style `0x1608` at `(12,18)`. Both raw
glyph-code byte sequences, including their zero-valued trailing glyphs, are
exported in `build/willow_story.h` as native data. The writer maps each byte to
a Scroll 1 glyph tile, so these strings are not ordinary ASCII. The interim
prompt scene now renders both records with their source glyph data and palette
group 6 alongside map `0x06`'s group-0 prompt. It preserves the encoded line
positions. The native controller now waits 240 frames before the first line
(180 for the first actor plus 60 for the second actor), 10 frames before the
second line, and 30 frames after it. Those values are checked against the
instructions at `0x82c6`, `0x83bc`, `0x8486`, and `0x84d4`. The native text
palettes use a 15-frame brightness ramp matching the source fade worker's
`0x1000` increment cadence. The source tasks `0x1012`–`0x1018` process
selected 16-color groups in those increments; exact title palette data and
group selection still need verification. The two timed actor entrances and
exact title composition remain to be ported.
The state-zero setup calls `0x0ac4`, which selects four setup words from the
table at `0x0a82` using `a5+0x0343`, then copies color blocks from ROM
`0xe9920` (or `0xe9d20` for a nonzero selector), `0xe72a0`, `0xeb700`, and
`0xe5280` into CPS palette RAM at `0x91c800`, `0x91c400`, `0x91cc00`, and
`0x91c200`.
The first three copies are 0x400 bytes each; the last is 0x200 bytes. Their
copy routine and byte spans are checked in the catalog. Task `0x1000` scans
`0x91c000`–`0x91cfff` plus `0x91d000`–`0x91d0ff` and
`0x91d400`–`0x91d4ff`: four 1 KiB blocks and two 256-byte blocks. Its helper
tests each 16-color group's first word, updates all 16 color words in that
group by `0x1000`, and updates the source completion mask. The full title art
and palette use remain
unidentified.

## Reverse-engineering notes

Static disassembly shows the animation selector at CPU ROM address `0x1f30`:
it indexes a relative-offset table using an object field, selects a frame
sequence, and initializes its frame timer. Willow routines call it with tables
at `0xd07e` and `0xd086`; these contain the walk and idle poses already used by
the prototype. Direct references in the player routines also identify tables
at `0xd1a2`, `0xd1aa`, `0xd1b2`, `0xd1b6`, `0xd2ca`, `0xd2ce`, `0xd3be`, and
`0xd3c2`. The catalog now preserves these additional raw records by address;
their gameplay meanings and sprite compositions still need verification. The
first two sequences contain six six-tick records. Their first five tile codes
are `0, 3, 6, 9, 12`; the final record selects frame base `0x30` and its control
word loops to the sequence start. The descriptor flags differ by
`0x20`, which MAME's CPS-1 renderer identifies as horizontal flip. The native
prototype follows that timing and loop, including the transparent beat. The
same analysis located
the source palette block at `0x0e5080`, copied by startup code into CPS graphics
RAM. The runtime viewer currently exposes its 32 16-color groups for inspection.
`make animation-catalog` applies the record stride and indirection rules from
`0x1f4c`, finds direct `lea table(pc),a0` references followed by `jsr` or
`jmp $1f30` in the offline
68000 image, and catalogs plausible contiguous relative-offset sequences with
their call-site addresses. Those inferred table lengths remain candidates for
manual validation. It saves the raw data to `build/willow_animations.json` and
emits validated Willow walk, idle, down-pose, `0xe194` selector-1 player,
`0x1116e` enemy, and `0xd2ca` jump and enemy attack metadata to
`build/willow_walk.h`. The table is retained as source data and is not applied
to the Stage 0 player. Other cataloged tables provide source-backed
leads for additional enemy and boss animations. The enemy handler at `0x1010e`
selects `0x1116e` for its six-frame directional idle animation; its `0x10186`
state checks proximity every four frames, and the approach state subtracts seven
from Y each update. The attack state selects `0x11226`, whose two directions
have nine timed records and an indefinite terminal pose; its frame codes,
dimensions, flips, and durations are now exported. The prototype advances the
approaching enemy by the exact seven-unit source step, then applies the center
surface snap and bit-3 property test from `0x40a0`, the return-producing check
used by `0x3b0a`, before selecting the attack pose. Its separate facing-side
solid check at `0x4190` is also modeled as the object's contact flag. Dynamic
profile selection remains to be ported; the negative shape-bit-6 path now
repeats its lookup after applying the first surface correction, as `0x40a0`
does. The complete `0x3b0a` probe profiles,
enemy damage, and player hurt response
remain unfinished. Further tracing of the same
object handler found its state table at `0x1016a`. The state-zero path checks
object coordinates at offsets `+6` and `+10` against work-area coordinates at
`A5+0x0408` and `A5+0x040c`, with limits `0x01a0` and `0x0100`, on a
four-frame cadence. A later branch selects the separate table at `0x11226`;
its two mirrored sequences have nine timed frames and an indefinite terminal
record. The transition is conditional: the handler advances its state, calls
`0x3b0a`, and selects `0x11226` only when that call returns nonzero. The helper
tests movement offsets from the table at `0x3b66` through the map address
calculation at `0x3e28` and collision routines at `0x4190`/`0x40a0`. Therefore
the sequence cannot be triggered accurately from player distance alone; the
native stage collision map and return conditions are still needed. The
internal dispatcher at `0xc8f2` selects handlers by object field `+4`; its
state-zero path initializes fields, advances `+4`, and falls through at
`0xc92e` to select the `0xd2ca` direction variant. The next timed states select
`0xd2ce`. After the state handler, the dispatcher calls `0xc6c0` (the shared
charge and class-2 child update) and tail-jumps to `0xc786` (the X-only
`0x20b4` vector helper) on every tick. Its later `0xc9da` path checks the
button-2 edge, updates jump state, probes `0x38f6`, and continues through
`0xc72e`. Those internal links are byte-validated, but the catalog scans the
assembled CPU image for direct branches/calls and literal pointer words to
`0xc8f2` and finds none. So the coherent path still has no proven caller from
the active Stage 0 actor. The verified Stage 0 actor dispatches through `0xffc8` to `0x125d0`,
whose state-zero path reaches normal-state entry `0x12780`. Genesis B triggers
the separately modeled `0xc78a` jump route; the `0xc8f2` animation route is
still not linked to that actor, and runtime-computed dispatch remains possible.

## Remaining port work

- Replace the interim source-backed Start prompt with the complete title and
  attract scene, including its initial system task, palette fade, timed actors,
  text sequence, and menu states before entering Stage 0 gameplay.
- Decode further `0x1f30` animation records and recover enemy and boss sprite
  compositions, timing, and CPS tile mappings.
- Reproduce the palette-derived Scroll 1 diagnostic overlay at `0x425a6` as a
  transient effect in a native Test-mode UI state; it is not a Stage 0 actor or
  persistent stage layer.
- Trace ordinary Stage 0 writes to Scroll 1 and the source foreground/HUD
  call paths before integrating any additional layer content.
- Recover original palettes, stage tilemaps, scroll behavior, collision rules,
  player/enemy state machines, hitboxes, item and boss logic, and level timing.
- Continue porting the Stage 0 player state machine from handler `0x125d0`.
  The fixed controller target vectors and Willow's actor-selected movement
  row are source-traced; native D-pad input moves the target, while Willow
  selects row 0/1 from her position relative to it. Genesis B enters the
  separately verified `0xc78a` jump route.
  Collision-triggered hurt behavior and the internal `0xc8f2` route remain
  unresolved.
- Identify the sound IDs used for voices and effects, map them to native game
  events, convert the music, and profile the mixed XGM arrangement on hardware.
- Implement the game loop, player controls, combat, enemies, stage progression,
  and UI entirely in native 68000 code.
- Compare captures against arcade reference play and verify the ROM on hardware.

The source data establishes graphics pixels and sample waveforms, but does not
itself explain the full game semantics. MAME's Willow driver and CPS-1 video layout are useful
hardware references: [Willow ROM map and input notes](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1.cpp),
[CPS-1 graphics layouts](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1.cpp#L3837),
and [CPS-1 tile address behavior and WL24B map](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1_v.cpp#L732).
The sample decoder follows MAME's [OKI6295 sample playback](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/devices/sound/okim6295.cpp)
and [OKI ADPCM state](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/devices/sound/okiadpcm.cpp) behavior.

The Stage 0 path through `0xa0f4` reaches setup at `0xa128`, which writes
Willow's world position `(192, 512)` and enters `0x78b8`. That helper queues
sound words `0x0013` and `0x02fa` through `0x783c`; the queue consumer at
`0x7800` sends each low byte to the Z80 sound-command port and each high byte
to the CPS-1 fade port. Command `0x13` resolves through the sound tables to cue
`0x8f90` (bank 1 ROM offset `0xcf90`). The second word sends fade command
`0xfa` with fade-timer value `0x02`; handler `0x03af` clears its fade counter,
stores this interval, and updates the sound-volume accumulator every two
ticks. Fade direction depends on existing sound-CPU state and is not
established for this entry sequence. Cue `0x8f90` track playback is still
unresolved. The
initializer block has no object allocator call; it does not rule out an enemy
created later by stage events.
The audio catalog now byte-validates this normal Stage 0 route through
`0x78b8` and its `0x7818` command-queue writer. It records queued words
`0x0013` and `0x02fa`, resolves `0x13` to cue `0x8f90`, and retains the
source track pointers for follow-up decoding. The Z80 loader at `0x01fa`
copies eight little-endian pointers after the cue header byte; the playback
reader at `0x0b26` dereferences those exact addresses. For cue `0x8f90`, the
nonzero pointers are `0xff06`, `0x004d`, `0xe100`, `0x0009`, `0x0600`, and
`0x4dff`. This confirms the unusual targets come from the source header, not
from a byte-order guess in the offline catalog. The CPS-1 sound CPU map places
`0xe100` and `0xff06` in unmapped space; `0x004d`, `0x0009`, `0x0600`, and
`0x4dff` are fixed-ROM addresses, while the cue header itself is in the banked
ROM window. The map exposes sound RAM only at `0xd000`–`0xd7ff` and YM2151,
OKI, bank, and latch registers at selected `0xf000`–`0xf00a` addresses
([MAME `sub_map`](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/capcom/cps1.cpp#L581-L591)).
The track update loop at `0x0453` skips a slot only when its pointer is zero;
all six nonzero slots enter the track handler, including `0xe100` and
`0xff06`. MAME's `address_map` default read value is zero, and Willow's sound
submap does not override it, so the first read at either unmapped pointer is
`0x00` in the MAME reference path. That byte dispatches through control-event
table entry 0 to handler `0x0972`, which fetches another byte from the track
pointer. The catalog validates both the table target and handler bytes, and
records this as MAME behavior only; physical open-bus behavior is unverified.
The first control-event call consumes a zero operand from the next unmapped
address and stores note-table pointer `0x1000` to `0xd015` or `0xd017`,
according to sound-RAM selector `0xd01a`. What happens after the pointer
advances on those two tracks, and what the source intended them to do, remain
unresolved. The fixed-ROM track at `0x4dff` is now decoded through 308 note,
timing, and control events to the source cue terminator at `0x4f75`. Its
instrument events select 40-byte OPM patches `0x03`, `0x07`, `0x0c`, `0x16`,
`0x18`, `0x1b`, `0x2c`, and `0x47`; these records are exported for native
conversion. Tracks at `0x004d`, `0x0009`, and `0x0600` still stop at extended
control events `0x11`, `0x18`, and `0x17`. Native cue playback still needs
driver-state/control-flow tracing and YM2151-to-YM2612 conversion, so the build
does not substitute guessed music. Track 6's event `0x17` computes destination
`0xcb3c`, inside unmapped sound-CPU space. The catalog now records the MAME
zero-read opcode path from `0xcb3c` through `0xcfff` (1,220 Z80 NOP fetches)
and stops at mapped sound RAM at `0xd000`; it makes no claim about execution
after that boundary. This is a reference-path trace, not proof of physical
open-bus behavior or of intended track data.
For cue `0x33` track 2, the catalog also validates the stream suffix
`4d 21 00 d0 11` before extended event `0x11`. If note `0x4d` reaches the
YM-write path, its verified register helper leaves `C=1`; timing event `0x21`
and control event `0x00` preserve that register, so the candidate handler's
`INC C` produces 2 and its `JR Z` is not taken. The rest of this overlapping
dispatch target remains unresolved, and this conditional trace does not yet
provide native playback.
The nearby `0xa198` type-2 allocation is not evidence for an initial Stage 0
enemy: control reaches it only when the stage counter at `a5+0x344` equals 3
and the event flag at `a5+0x3a0` is clear. It creates behavior 7 at
`(-96,4200)`, on the separate branch that resets world position to `(192,4096)`.
The object catalog now validates this branch and its gate from the ROM bytes.
The adjacent counter-4 branch allocates behaviors 32, 34, and 33 at
`0xa1d6`, `0xa1e6`, and `0xa202`. Behavior 33 later allocates a child with
byte `+32 = 37`; these values lie beyond the verified 35-entry dispatcher
table, so their runtime dispatch remains unresolved. They are not used as
Stage 0 enemy spawns.
The Stage 0 initializer at `0xa28a` allocates an active type-2 actor and sets
its world coordinates to `(218,136)`; it then creates an active type-1 actor
at `(160,80)` at `0xa2a6`, matching Willow's screen anchor. The type-2 actor's
position is consistent with Stage 0 world coordinates: compared with Willow's
initial world `(192,512)`, its Y is 376 pixels above her and outside the
scheduler's nonnegative `dy` window. Its type-1 player actor has byte `+32 = 3`,
which dispatches through `0xffa2` to native-source handler `0x125d0`. The pool
clear at `0x266c` leaves the actor's initial state fields zero. The normal
Stage 0 route reaches these allocations after the seven-tick state-8 wait and
63-tick state-10 wait. This validated 70-tick schedule matches the native
opening delay that activates the player and linked actor. The handler's initial
path at `0x1261c` selects animation table `0x13154`, sets its timer to
one, and advances its substate. The next handler entry at `0x1262e` sets
collision profile 3 and points object field `+24` at the signed 8.8 vector
table `0x136b0`; normal states 1–5 call `0x208c` before `0x3b0a`. This
player-handler entry path is now identified
separately from the native prototype's manually selected walk, jump, and charge
states, but its complete state machine is not yet ported. The player's first
normal-state update at `0x12780` changes state `+3` from 0 to 2, sets a
64-tick timer, resolves facing with `0x12d44`, and selects the `0x13154`
animation. State 2 dispatches through `0x127a0`; its substate-zero path applies
stored motion, calls `0x3b0a` for collision resolution, and tests byte +31. A
clear byte enters state 4 before animation advance; a set byte advances the
active animation and checks the Y band relative to the shared target before
calling the `0x12ede` timer. Handler `0x12d6e` selects substate 2 below -48,
substate 4 above +48, and substate 0 across the inclusive `[-48,+48]` band.
The runtime now subtracts `a5+0x1850` from Willow's world Y and preserves those
exact boundaries; the animation catalog byte-checks the selector. The vector
table is therefore part of the normal player handler, not only its hurt
response: `0x1262e` installs it before the first normal-state update, and the
facing update at `0x12f30` selects vector index 0 or 1 by comparing player X
with the normal-path Stage 0 target X, initially zero in arcade coordinates
(native x=32 after the camera translation). The fixed input controller's
validated target motion is independent of Willow's actor motion. Willow uses
the target-derived 0/1 vector selected at normal-state timer expiry; rows 2
and 3 remain reserved for other player states. The
native state 2 now follows the source's 64-tick timer from `0x12780`. Routine
`0x12ede` reloads it from the 16-byte table at `0x12f18`, indexes one of eight
masks at `0x12f20` using bits 5–7 of the counter low byte, and enters state 4
on a set LFSR bit. Vertical-band changes between state-2 substates 0, 2, and 4
skip that update's timer call, as in the source handlers. The vertical selector
is byte-validated at `0x12d6e`; the timer tables and lookup sequence at
`0x12ee8` are also byte-validated by the offline animation catalog. The native
path shares the CPS LFSR and enters top-level state 4 on the next update.
Normal movement follows the fixed controller's moving target;
Genesis B enters the separately modeled Stage 0 jump path. State 4 refreshes facing
from the shared target on both timer and side-contact entry. A side-contact
hit branches before the source animation advance, so the native walk/idle
frame timers now pause on that transition tick.
The previously connected `+0x0400` ballistic simulation is not the normal
top-level state-4 route at `0x1284a`; no verified Stage 0 path connects its
`0x1308c` entry to Willow's state-2 side-contact, timer, or state-8 exit. Those
events now enter the source-verified ordinary state-4 movement path instead.
The ballistic trace remains separate pending a verified caller. The native
player frame stream now uses the source
`0x19dfe` codes, dimensions, origins, facing bits, and 2/2/16-tick holds; the
`0x19e02` substate-4 pose is also selected. Its `0x3bc6` check now follows
the class-3 facing flag and shape-threshold branch in `0x42fa`.
The player state-4 substate-6 route at `0x130e0` allocates a queue-class-14
actor through `0x2508`. It sends event `0x1800`, advances the shared LFSR,
and selects descriptor 1 or 2 from the table at `0x13120`. Helper `0x2508`
resolves those descriptors to actor byte `+33` values 2 or 5, then calls the
`0x2bea` allocator for the 60-record, 64-byte pool initialized at `0x28da`.
The actor inherits parent coordinates and byte `+47`; byte `+46` is zero.

The pool scheduler at `0x2cf8e` visits all 60 physical slots in ascending
order and dispatches byte `+32` through its own table at `0x2cfb6`. For these
spawns, `+32=0` selects `0x2cfc2`, which dispatches states 0, 2, 4, and 6 to
`0x2cfea`, `0x2d0aa`, `0x2d22c`, and `0x2d2e8`. The state-0 handler sets up
animation from `+33`, initializes vertical velocity to 768, derives horizontal
velocity from `+46` (zero for this spawn), and starts a 16-tick phase. State 2
runs its own substate table, shared actor update, and visibility callback.
Callback `0x2244` applies the screen bounds and puts `+14=0` actors at the head
of the class-14 render list. Because the source scheduler visits slots upward,
the native renderer's descending pool scan preserves the same visible order.
State 4 handles target following and timed
animation; state 6 releases the record through `0x2c06`. The allocator,
capacity, scheduler, and behavior-0 dispatch bytes are validated in
`build/willow_objects.json`.

**Native fidelity gap:** `src/main.c` now uses the 60-slot queue-class-14
pool, initializes state 0, models the state-2 vertical phases and `0x3c48`
terrain gate, applies the source 3/4 velocity decay and `+48` horizontal step,
and handles state-4 follow/retirement timers. The 300-update transition now
accounts for the arcade handler checking `+52` before its common-tail
increment. Its alternating `0x3c48`/`0x6e44` branch now uses the source phase:
the scheduler visits physical slots upward while D7 counts down from 59, making
`(frame + D7 + 1) & 1` equivalent to `(frame + slot) & 1`. It also draws the
extracted state-0/state-4 frames and the 3-frame `0x2d2ec` transition
animation. The earlier selector-2/5 enemy behavior model was removed from this
pool. The native runtime also models the `0x488a` overlap call after each
state-2 substate handler. Its every-eight-frame phase follows the source
scheduler's D7 countdown, and its unsigned 16-bit rectangle comparison uses
row 0 from `0x3b1c2`, selected by the static target record at `0xd14a`.
Overlap enters state 4, substate 0, which reaches the existing target-follow
path on the next update. The `0x6e44` branch effects, target-list handoff, and
state-4 sound sequence remain incomplete. State-2 dispatch at `0x2d0aa` has
table entries only for substates 0, 2, and 4; the verified transitions write
only those values. Substate 6 would read beyond the table into unrelated code,
and no normal Stage 0 writer to it has been established. The recovery path now
models the separate class-12 child’s selector-5 32-tick
state-2 timer and its state-6 pool release on the following active update. The
sequenced command `0x33` audio effect still needs an accurate native playback
path. The native build is not an accurate port until these paths and the
remaining animation states are implemented.

The optional `0x2d0f0` camera-edge reflection reads global byte `a5+0x03cf`.
Its writer at `0x27f08` runs only when the surrounding actor's byte `+42` is
zero; it enters state 2 and attempts a queue-class-6 behavior-6 allocation.
Those writer bytes are now validated in `build/willow_objects.json`, but the
writer's owning actor has no established route from normal Stage 0 setup, so
the native class-14 path leaves this gate inactive.

The queue-class-14 state-4 target-follow entry at `0x2d242` sends sequenced
sound command `0x2d` before positioning the child at the shared target. The
audio catalog now validates this exact dispatch and call site. Command `0x2d`
selects cue data at `0x8eea`; the native sequencer still does not play it.
The same entry calls `0x4e12` with selector indexes 2 or 5. That helper adds
the packed-BCD amounts 20 or 200 to the eight-digit score, and calls twice when
the child inherits parent flag +47. The native path now applies those awards
and rejects additions that overflow the source's eight-digit score field. The
award table and both call sites are source-byte validated.

The animation catalog now extracts the actual class-14 streams. State 0's
selector-2 loop is four 4-tick frames (`0x06f8`–`0x06fb`); selector 5 uses
`0x06fc`, `0x06fd`, `0x0731`, and `0x0730`. After the 300-tick state-2 path,
the source selects `0x2d2ec`, a three-frame animation (`0x0736`, `0x0bda`,
`0x0bd8`) held for four ticks per frame, with source dimensions 2×1, 2×2,
2×2. The separate state-4 selection table resolves selectors 2/5 and
parent-link variants 14/17 to held poses `0x0735` or `0x0732`. These codes,
dimensions, origins, and holds are emitted in `build/willow_walk.h`; the
renderer uses them for state 2 and state 4. The generator also resolves the
source coordinate templates at `0x3b99a` for origins 0, 1, 8, and 12. The
native renderer uses those exact offsets for the base frames and each appended
held-pose code. Other state transitions remain incomplete.

The separate queue-class-4 enemy handler also has a top-level state-4 route:
`0x10054` dispatches state `+2=4` through `0x10eea`, and its common update
returns through `0x2244`. The transition at `0x10c32` requires global lock

and either clears the substate or enters a `+0x0400` vector/recovery route.
The queue-class-14 recovery actors use a different scheduler and do not run
this class-4 state machine.
The handler block initializes both to 1 at `0x102a8` and contains no later
direct write to `+42`. A superficially matching writer at `0x116c0` belongs to
class-4 handler selector 1 (`0x115ee`, dispatcher slot 1 at `0xffcc`); the

The state-4 recovery timer also emits a distinct actor at `0x130ba`. After

This makes that scripted writer inactive on the verified normal Stage 0 path
unless an aliased write exists. The other writer is the separate descriptor-based state-4 handler at
`0x2d89a`; it loads the fields from its selector-indexed data table.
The recovery-created queue-class-14 actor sets handler selector `+32=0` and

through that dispatch entry. The `0x2d89a` creator and substate-4 reachability remain
unresolved, so its coordinates are not used by the native runtime. This record
is separate from both the class-2 charge pool and the queue-class-14 actors above. The callsite,
allocators, dispatch entry, handler bytes, and the two conditional phase-field
writers are checked by `player_state4_class12_spawn` in

code now allocates from a 60-record class-12 free stack, stores the computed
phase result `0xd0`, and applies actor coordinates `(0x3b40,0x8a32)`. The actor
is beyond the Stage 0 map, runs its verified 32-tick state-2 timer, and returns
to the free stack on the next state-6 update; it has no native render entry. The sequenced command
`0x33` and non-Stage-0 lookup inputs remain unimplemented; the native runtime
applies the verified `0x3940` shared retirement threshold, so existing Stage 0
culling consumers see the same bound. This reproduction does not classify the
code-byte result as an intended enemy.

The sound catalog now traces the verified `0x33` call at main-CPU address
`0x11da4` through the complete active track-7 stream: 308 events end at cue
terminator `0x0f` at sound-ROM offset `0x4f74`. That pass finds eight selected
instrument records (`0x03`, `0x07`, `0x0c`, `0x16`, `0x18`, `0x1b`, `0x2c`,

stop at unresolved extended control events (`0x11`, `0x18`, and `0x17`), so
this trace is source data for a future native sequencer, not cue playback.
Command `0x33` and startup command `0x13` share sequence address `0x8f90`.
The reset Stage 0 inputs now have a byte-validated static evaluation: the
handler reads `0xd0` from code at `0x385c`, raises phase byte `a5+0x394` to

The opening Stage 0 actor at `0xa28a` is in the 60-record class-12 pool
initialized at `0x2756`, not the separate 50-record class-4 pool at `0x266c`.
The main object dispatcher at `0xffa2` routes its behavior selector 1 through

drawing message `0x2e`. Native `stage0OpeningTimer` uses the same 70-tick delay
before activating the player and linked actor, and a separate message timer
now reproduces the task's 29-tick delay. The scripted camera Y transition
still starts after the 70-tick controller route. The animation catalog now

the camera. It also validates that states 4 and 6 route to pool cleanup at

holds into `willow_walk.h`. Native code now streams those uncompressed CPS
frames into VRAM and renders the actor as Genesis sprites. This corrects the
previously misattributed `0x115ee` patrol, proximity, lunge, and voice model;

The source state-2 handler calls helper `0x21c6` every 16 global updates for
this first allocated record. Its Stage 0 branch retires the actor when its X
falls below the global lower bound at `a5+0x038c`. Camera update routine
`0x42602` loads its camera target from `a5-0x8fb0/-0x8fb2` when the normal Stage
0 flag `a5+0x0348` is clear. The initializer sets those fields to `(192,640)`,

remain unresolved. Update routine `0x4281e` calls the tracker at `0x42924`,

catalog now byte-validates the publisher, tracker dispatch and Stage 0 path,
and lower-bound helper. Helper `0x42e4e` advances the lower bound by taking

zero. The tracker uses a 192-pixel horizontal offset between target
field `+106` and camera position `+6`, then clamps camera motion against fields

Stage 0 value is `0x07a0`. This identifies the source endpoint consumed by the
tracker. The active phase-zero camera center is 192, while the native player
anchor is 160, so the native scroll coordinate is the source camera coordinate
plus 32. Direct A5-relative
references show the normal initializer at `0xa11c`, the alternate
stage-counter initializer at `0xa162`, and a scripted Y decrement at `0xa2fe`.
Full main-CPU disassembly finds no later direct write to the normal-path target
X `a5-0x8fb0`; routine `0x4261a` copies that constant `192` into camera object
+106. While `a5+0x0348` is set, `0x42602` instead loads object +106 from shared
controller target `a5+0x184c`. The source therefore has two camera X modes: a
fixed 192 target in normal mode and a controller-driven target in flagged mode.
The stage catalog now byte-validates both source-selection branches, the
`max(target X - 192, lower bound)` tracker step, and camera-update calls at
`0x947e`, `0x9634`, and `0x3b524`. Computed or aliased writes remain possible.
It now also validates the complete 900-tick phase handler through its tail jump
to `0x3b524`, which reaches the camera updater and tracker while the Stage 0
phase is active. The normal-mode vertical follow routine at `0x42b3e` is now
byte-validated and confirms the two-pixel-per-tick response to the scripted
Stage 0 target decrement. Horizontal live target tracking remains a separate
source path: the normal target X writer and the routine's active caller have

dispatcher `0x8cb4` and table `0x8cc0`: state 0 enters `0x8cda`, advances the
state word by two, and the next dispatch reaches `0x8da8`. That handler sets
the flag and starts the 900-tick phase. The dispatcher and table bytes are
checked by the stage catalog. The caller that activates this state record in

The stage setup routine `0x2f8a` writes fields `a5+0x0370/+0x0372` as
`(0x00c0,0x0048)` before normal Stage 0 initialization. The initializer at

helper's `max(previous, camera X - 768)` rule. The live target/lag behavior
and caller for flagged camera mode remain approximate. The stage catalog
validates the setup, dispatch, resolver, pointer table, and selected record.
The known target-Y mutation at `0xa2fe` is guarded by nonzero player world Y
at `a5+0x040c`; it subtracts 2, calls `0x9ef2`, then transfers to `0x3b524`.
The normal Stage 0 state path is now linked: state 6 at `0xa0d0` falls through
to the ordinary initializer, which advances to state 8; state 8 runs 7 ticks,
state 10 runs 63 ticks, and state 12 reaches the guarded Y update. The catalog
byte-validates the dispatcher entries and each transition. Native camera Y
now starts the same two-pixel-per-tick scroll after the 70-tick opening delay,
stops the target decrement when Willow's world Y reaches zero, stops at the
stage's lower camera bound, and offsets screen-space actors to preserve their
world coordinates while the viewport moves. The camera update
dispatcher at `0x42b1c` selects normal mode `0x42b3e`, which applies the
128-pixel target deadband to camera object fields `+108` (target Y) and `+10`
(camera Y). With Stage 0's initial source values 640 and 512, the first
scripted target decrement makes the camera follow at -2 pixels per tick, as

anchor translation, uses signed bounds `-80..464`, and draws blank map cells
above source world Y=0. This preserves the source lower-bound timing: both
cameras take 256 two-pixel updates to reach their lower limit. The stage
catalog checks the initializer bytes and derives these translated bounds from
