### Original task startup boundaries

`willow_arcade_task_startup.h` translates the primary queue initialization at
1400, the separate secondary-buffer entry at 1424, and the conditional fixed
task starts at 14AC. The first entry reaches 1436 through BSR 142E without
returning through 1424 at that boundary. It clears the four index words and
fills FF8072..FF8171 with FFFF; the separate entry zeros FF8172..FF8271.
The fixed starts preserve inherited D1/D2 parameters and existing active tasks,
starting slot 0 at 7FDA and slot A0 at 1DDC only when inactive.

`make test-arcade-task-startup` executes the corresponding original instructions
with the real trap-0 handler in headless libretro. All 8,192 cases pass under
fatal address/undefined-behavior sanitizers. Checks cover both buffer entries,
eight initial task states, inherited parameters, exit PC/SP, queue exit
registers, and every RAM byte outside the explicitly excluded stack scratch
range EFC0..F003. Evidence: `build/source-task-startup.log`.

The same test covers the ten-record pool initialization at 1466..148E:
FFEFC6..FFF015 receives the 80 original bytes at 183C; FFF016..FFF03D
receives ten pointers, and FFF03E receives the original first longword.
The helper preserves the full supplied A5 pointer representation. The test
alternates 00FF8000 and boot's sign-extended FFFF8000 and checks all RAM
without any stack exclusion for this call-free entry. It stops at 1490 before
the separately verified task free-list initialization.

This test stops at the external startup-service and interrupt-enable boundaries.
It does not establish the complete boot call chain or initialize the native
game. In particular, main task 7FDA remains unsupported by the native task
runtime, and startup-service ordering still needs translation before integration.
No GUI was opened or diagnostic ROM replaced.

### Boot manager handlers and option decoding

`willow_arcade_boot_state.h` translates the six handlers dispatched through
7FF4 by main task 7FDA, plus the three return points within handler 8010.
It preserves the original RNG seed, manager state changes, two command
enqueues, 16-bit countdown wrap, and conditional fixed-task handoff to 80D0
or 45A8C. Calls to other services are explicit returned boundaries, with
their original continuation address where applicable. A requested service
must execute before resuming; particularly, the fade wait at 1E88 cannot be
treated as an immediate return. Task termination at 1636 is also a boundary.

`willow_arcade_boot_options.h` translates 1AC2, 1B46 and 1B96, reading their
original tables from ROM and modifying only the corresponding option state.
It uses already-latched input bytes; it does not replace the physical input
read at 1A68. The boot-state oracle has a mode that runs these three real
services end to end instead of stopping at their entry points.

`make test-arcade-boot-state` checks 18,432 boundaries in each mode under
fatal sanitizers. Original table dispatch, real command producer, and real
trap-0 fixed-task starts execute in both modes. Cases cover all queue offsets,
countdowns including zero/one/FFFF, active task states, both handoff branches,

### Boot task continuation through nested waits

`willow_native_boot_task.h` composes the boot handlers and option services
into a continuation of task 7FDA. Its eight-byte state retains the current PC,
nested wait return address and live D1/D2 words. Command enqueue changes D2
to the updated queue offset; preserving that register is necessary for exact
parameters on the eventual fixed-task handoff. The initial 1E88 wait returns
to 7FDE, while the later handler's tail wait returns to 7FEA and must still
perform the normal one-tick main-loop sleep before the next dispatch.

The helper also translates 1E72's status-bit update and returns sleep or
termination requests. It does not itself wake, release or allocate a scheduler
slot. ROM data at 7FF4 still selects each boot handler; invalid manager states
are reported unsupported rather than mapped to a substitute handler.

`test-native-boot-task` runs original boot instructions, option services,
command producer and fixed-task traps, intercepting only sleep entry 1750 and
termination entry 1636. Across 19,860 sleep/finish boundaries and 1,452
handoffs, live D1/D2, sleep duration, original return PC and all RAM outside
stack scratch EF80..F003 match. Cases start at initial entry or each manager
state, exercise every queue offset and option byte, repeated pending waits,
countdown wrap and active/inactive handoff slots. Fatal sanitizers pass.
Evidence: `build/native-boot-task.log`.

Completion flags are controlled test inputs, not an implementation of the
queued commands. Sleep is resumed by restoring its caller PC/SP in the oracle;
this test does not establish scheduler/interrupt timing. The helper remains
separate from the native runtime pending that integration and memory-budget
verification. Full gameplay, the subsequent tasks and full-frame timing remain
unverified. No emulator GUI was opened or diagnostic ROM changed.

### Boot's fade-and-clear command

`willowArcadeTransitionClear` translates command 0C00's handler at 5858 and
its continuations 586E/58DA. It enqueues the original global fade-out command,
always sleeps once, and waits for the original dark-state word. Once dark it
writes 4,096 tile/attribute pairs to each of the three CPS tilemaps (7020/0,
0000/0 and 0A00/0 respectively), clears 829C/829E, and zeros both 2,048-byte
object buffers. It then sleeps for the byte argument plus four before clearing
FFF891 and finishing. The delay is a word: arguments 252..255 produce
256..259, preserving the source sleep service's low-byte semantics later.

clear rejects a missing callback before changing RAM; it cannot silently
declare a transition complete without applying the renderer effects.

uses source 2634C vectors and 261F0 images. The initial WORD countdown is distinct
from later BYTE timers. Orbit movement accumulates full signed vector offsets,
then publishes only integer positions relative to globals 83F0/83F2, retaining
actor position fractions. Direction updates use original 128-direction wrapping,
the decreasing turn increment and the parent direction-change flip.

The word lifetime expires into the original 20D2 player-direction calculation;
rounding adds two with byte wrap before shifting by two. Live D4 is retained or
changed exactly by the direction helper's axis/diagonal/general paths. Parent
handles are WORD values sign-extended into A4. Parent byte 104 or main state at
least four causes immediate release before animation/visibility. Departure uses
source movement, floor and bounds checks and intentionally steps animation twice
per update (inside the substate and again in the common tail).

Release decrements shared word FF0EC2 and clears byte FF83F4 only when that word
becomes zero, then performs class-ten pool release. No pause gate is invented.

16DF8, active dispatch 16E90, damage propagation 16EF2, death dispatch 1705E and
initial effect helper 16F4C. Initialization selects one of 24 source movement
scripts and the caller-provided image table. Active movement occurs before
reading the next duration/direction pair; only variant bit one enables ordinary
animation stepping. Negative direction terminates without saving the advanced
script pointer. The outer damage check can override that same-call retirement.

The scene flag overrides every variant. Otherwise variant zero responds to its
own changed health; linked variants respond to the next object's death flag.
Death waits for the next object's completion flag before a six-call countdown,
then publishes its own completion and emits the original effect. The initial
effect is attempted only for path indices divisible by four.

22984, health 229B4 and death 22A00. Setup preserves health ten, ED078 motion,
field clears, palette five, collision mode five, signed wrapped player-facing
and the original image before floor querying. The settling substate lowers
integer Y by three until existing contact advances the phase. Admission uses
inclusive X +/-160, the original RNG count table and a word-wide contact clear.
Outside that range it preserves motion, integer Y-2, terrain and animation order.
Only the final entry substate queues visibility.

Nonlethal health changes acknowledge health, select palette fourteen, initialize
fifteen-call recovery and queue sound 50; lethal health advances main state and
clears both substates. Recovery execution itself is not yet integrated. Normal
death queues sound 51, uses the source RNG reward table and event 1806 with the
reward displacement as its live argument. Stage-exit death skips those steps.
Both paths set activity two, advance state, attempt the variant-five effect and
queue visibility.

The direct fixture passed 65,536 original non-stack RAM/D4/A4 comparisons under
ASan/UBSan across all entry substates, varied terrain, facing/proximity edges,

### Compiled 68000 gameplay execution (2026-10-04)

`tools/gameplay_runtime_probe.c` is a freestanding target-CPU integration
adapter for the complete translated Stage0 gameplay body and frame publication.
It calls the C implementations; it does not execute the original arcade logic
as its implementation. The original program executes separately as the oracle.
Build with `python3 tools/build_gameplay_runtime_probe.py` (SGDK defaults to
`/tmp/willow-sgdk-resume`, overridable with `SGDK`). This command builds only;
it never launches an emulator. The linker script reserves diagnostic globals
at cartridge SRAM 200800 and rejects initialized data or ROM/SRAM overflow.
The compiled text/constant image is approximately 467 KiB.

`WILLOW_TEST_NATIVE_TARGET` in `tools/test_arcade_stage0_full_frame.c` runs each
update three ways: host C translation, original arcade instructions, and the
compiled C on the emulated Genesis 68000. It restores identical input state
before the target run and compares observable RAM, both scroll layers, both
sprite buffers, modeled D4/A4, final sprite cursor and remaining budget. The
reference and target share the same headless core sequentially; no GUI runs.

The diagnostic is deliberately separate from the shipping runtime layout.
Source-layout gameplay RAM remains at FF0000. The C stack occupies the unused
6000..7FFF portion of the fixture's relocated text page, with SP initially
FF7F00. Each update first checks that original execution did not alter any byte
in that reserved range; target comparisons exclude only that verified-unused
range and the existing source oracle stack. This is not proof that the same
reservation is safe for every scene or task. Continuation/global state uses
36 bytes in the independent SRAM gap, separate from sprite and map regions.

Initial setup failures exposed two oracle-specific issues, which are fixed:
empty linker .data did not advance the .bss location, so .bss now has an explicit
SRAM address and the harness validates symbol ranges before indexing memory;
and native ROM reads must use untouched source data, not the hardware-relocated
oracle image. In particular, the charge-HUD pointer table at 5080 is patched
for original execution and cannot serve as native source data. The diagnostic
now retains pristine program/data at ROM 300000 and maps source data reads there.
The resulting 4 MiB cartridge explicitly enables SRAM via A130F1 before tests.
These are diagnostic layout corrections, not changes to arcade behavior.

The ASan/UBSan host harness passes 2,048 compiled-target updates across two
1,024-update input/weapon sequences. All three implementations match. Coverage:
1,433 normal-state Willow updates, source camera maximum X=1,330, 575 updates
with stage-spawned class4 actors (383 in active state), 23 player class2
allocations, 22 class8 allocations, three class12 allocations, and 4,251 sprite
pieces. Log: `build/native-gameplay-target.log`. The target is built with
`-m68000 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fno-builtin -ffreestanding`; no target
emulation/interpreter is used inside the translated code.

### Gameplay CPU budget and first optimizations (2026-10-04)

The target-mode full-frame harness accepts `--cycles`. It validates the core's
register layout and calibrates a NOP to 28 master cycles (four 68000 cycles),
then steps the compiled native update while collecting instruction costs and
minimum stack pointer. The NTSC budget is 3420 * 262 = 896,040 master cycles.
Bus refresh is included. VDP transfers/DMA, audio, shipping tile conversion and
outer scheduling are excluded; these numbers cannot establish sustained 60 FPS.
Per-instruction totals are written to `build/gameplay-cycle-profile.csv`.

The initial 2,048-update run passed behavioral comparisons but exceeded the
budget on 365 of 2,038 active updates. Active mean/max were 774,229/1,103,578
master cycles (`build/native-gameplay-cycles-baseline.log`). Eight of ten startup
updates also exceeded budget. This contradicts completion of the 60 FPS goal.

The freestanding diagnostic memcpy now copies even-aligned data with long/word
accesses, retaining byte handling for odd addresses and mismatched alignment.
GCC may_alias types permit these accesses across the copied structure types.
The change reduced active mean/max to 759,725/1,089,074 and budget misses to 263,
with all original/host/compiled comparisons passing
(`build/native-gameplay-cycles-copy.log`).

The shared player adapter now expands its fixed snapshot fields directly,
avoiding construction and traversal of address/pointer metadata on the stack.
Read order, write order and conditional commits remain unchanged; unchanged
fields still preserve service-callback writes. The final run passes all 2,048
three-way comparisons, with active mean/max 755,798/1,084,230 and 236 updates over
budget. Maximum observed C stack descent fell from 1,116 to 876 bytes. Startup
mean/max are 1,443,854/1,641,514, with eight of ten over budget. Log:
`build/native-gameplay-cycles-player-fields.log`. An independent sanitized
player-controller oracle also passes 24 routes * 4,096 = 98,304 cases with shared
RAM and D4/A4 comparisons (`build/arcade-player-direct-fields.log`). Adding the
may_alias annotation produced a byte-identical target binary to the tested one:
SHA256 `f89b55ed8b87627915d0776e034eac7449035a531de27c4643d747be9a92e265`.

These are incremental CPU and stack improvements, not a playable release or

### Resumable outer gameplay/event routing (2026-10-04)

The existing 9530..968E event router assumes synchronous service callbacks.
`src/willow_arcade_event_resume.h` adds a separate resumable interface for the
same original control flow. A two-byte task retains the source call/continuation
PC. Entry is selected only at invocation start; service callbacks return one
on completion, two on suspension, or zero when unsupported. Resuming calls the
same service with the same explicit argument until it completes. Services must
retain their own continuation state. Outer RAM writes and preceding calls are
not replayed, and later flag reads happen after the preceding service finishes.

The implementation follows the original instruction branches at 9530, 9600,
962E and 964C, including timeout precedence, removal/event/transition priority,
post-785E flag reads, countdown wraparound, and player restoration. It does not
supply a task scheduler, service bodies or a replacement event-completion rule.
The original synchronous API remains unchanged.

`make test-arcade-event-resume` uses the existing original-instruction routing
oracle with three callback modes: immediate completion, a wait before service
writes, and waits both before and after service writes. All 12,288 comparisons
pass, including 27,504 waits. Original service endpoints are instrumented to
record order, explicit arguments and state snapshots; deliberate callback
mutations test read-after-call ordering. Full non-stack RAM matches. These are
routing/service-boundary tests, not execution of actual service bodies during
suspension. Evidence: `build/arcade-event-resume.log`. The original synchronous
4,096-case test also passes (`build/arcade-event-route-compat.log`). Both use
fatal ASan/UBSan and warnings as errors. The new interface compiles for 68000
with strict freestanding flags (`build/event-resume-target.o`).

The new test is a native-player-input regression prerequisite. Binding this
router to the already translated gameplay and event services, retaining their
live registers through real scheduler waits, and proving the combined flow
remain necessary. Production ROM and prior gameplay timing results are
unchanged. No GUI was launched.

### Main gameplay task loop and scheduling gates (2026-10-04)

Source inspection distinguishes the main gameplay task at 92D2 from attract
phase 8DE4. Earlier references to a complete 8DE4 gameplay task in the scheduler
notes/test comment were corrected. At 92D2 the source waits on 1ECC(argument 1),
sets FFF9A1, checks the FF828F/FF8068 pause gate, increments only FF8019 before
93BE, and calls 18BC after that manager returns. It then checks the exit input,
debug variable-delay gate, and FFF9A1. A cleared FFF9A1 can cause another loop
iteration without a task sleep; otherwise the ordinary sleep is one tick.
Debug delays are exactly ((FF8067 & 30) >> 1) + 2 ticks.

explicit resumable service bindings. Manager/service suspension preserves the
call boundary, so input gates and the simulation increment are not replayed.

binding and must complete before the caller retires the task. This helper does
not replace manager 93BE, service 18BC, or exit behavior with placeholders.

### Main manager elapsed counter and ROM dispatch (2026-10-04)

`src/willow_arcade_gameplay_manager.h` translates the 938E elapsed counter
and the 93BE/93FE/9416 dispatch chain. The counter is skipped when manager
8000 is zero; otherwise its byte uses the original ABCD increment with cleared
extend. Values below 60 hex are stored; other results clear the byte and
increment the 16-bit counter, saturating its overflow at FFFF. This preserves
instruction behavior for invalid BCD input bytes as well as normal values.

State destinations are read from original ROM tables 93CC, 940A and 9422.
Thirteen resulting leaf entry points are handed to an explicit resumable
service. Their bodies are not fabricated or treated as automatically complete.
The selected address persists across suspension, preventing a repeated elapsed
increment or a different dispatch when a suspended leaf changes selectors.
Undocumented/odd table indices return unsupported rather than indexing arbitrary
ROM data. Further dispatch inside 942E, 96BE and 9748 is still leaf work.

### Lossless 14-bit map token representation (2026-10-04)

Added `willow_native_map14.h` as the representation needed to shrink the near
map's CPU cell array. Its 4,096 tokens occupy 3,584 words (7,168 bytes), versus
8,192 bytes for the current array. Tokens index the unchanged full 32-bit
code/attribute dictionary; mutable slots use the remaining token range. The
current dictionary has 9,069 entries, so every cell can additionally have its
own distinct mutable slot (4,096 slots) within the 16,384-token limit. Encoding
preserves the existing map store's 8000|slot API convention. Invalid cell/token
writes and invalid dictionary/override capacities are rejected without mutation.
No source color, tile code or attribute bits are quantized or discarded.

`make test-native-map14` exercises every token value, all cell positions,
contiguous/strided updates, first/last and cross-word boundaries, dictionary
and mutable-ID round trips and rejection without corruption. Independent
16-bit cell arrays are compared across the entire map after each random run.
All 95,816 write/ID round-trip checks pass with strict warnings, ASan and fatal
UBSan (`build/native-map14.log`).

This header is not yet connected to the existing map-store mutation/refcount
logic, collision reads, renderer or emulator-state audits. The 1,024-byte saving
is therefore potential, not recovered production RAM. Integration must retain
mutable-pair semantics and pass compiled emulator/pixel/timing checks before
it can replace the renderer's map cells. The current ROM and its 2,680-byte
free-heap measurement are unchanged; the full port remains incomplete.

### Division-free native column ring index (2026-10-04)

Continued investigating the rejected Map14 renderer. Reusing a converted source
pair across its two/four subtile rows within one column-publication call did not
remove the tick-966 walking failure. An independent immediate-input stress run
also reports a repeated update at 917, so the candidate cannot be dismissed as
only a mid-update snapshot issue. The pair cache and packed renderer remain
separate under `build/map14-pair-cache-candidate/`; they are not integrated in
the current ROM. Logs: `build/map14-pair-cache-walk.log` and
`build/map14-pair-cache-stress.log`. No camera or actor timing was relaxed.

Inspection found repeated native ring-index signed divisions. Retained a
representation-only optimization in `willowColumnSlot`: because 256 is -2
modulo 43, the signed high byte and unsigned low byte fold into [-254,511].
Adding 258 when negative, then conditionally subtracting 344/172/86/43 gives
the exact nonnegative residue without DIVS or multiplication. Forced inlining
avoids the new helper becoming an out-of-line call in the renderer.

Exhaustive host comparison covers every signed 16-bit argument against `%43`,
in addition to 360,448 window transitions (`build/column-window-fold.log`).
A new headless compiled-68000 probe runs both the folded and previous division
implementation for all 65,536 inputs, checks results and return-stack behavior,
and validates the core cycle-counter layout with a known 28-master-cycle NOP.
The folded function averages 1,178.17 master cycles, maximum 1,344; the previous
function averages 1,607.20, maximum 1,722. The folded version is faster for every
input, with 26.7% lower average cost. This is a function-call microbenchmark,
not a whole-frame speedup or proof of campaign 60 FPS.
Reproduce with `make test-native-column-slot-m68k SGDK_ROOT=/tmp/willow-sgdk-resume`;
evidence: `build/column-slot-m68k.log`. Probe sources:
`tools/native_column_slot_probe.c`, `tools/test_native_column_slot_m68k.c`.

The current ROM retains the dense near map plus this ring-index optimization.

slot indices, and source cursor words reflect the native cursor. Source word
writes translate valid original record handles back into indices and cursor
addresses back into slot positions. Count writes and record byte/word writes

handles/cursors, mismatched pool descriptors and out-of-range counts fail
without mutation. Unmapped globals and visibility queues remain the caller's

to those handle fields are explicitly unsupported, not silently approximated.

### Packed tile-index storage experiment: fits tasks, fails movement timing (2026-10-04)

Returned to production integration after the initial spawner coverage milestone.
The retired intro lookup already reserves the 52-byte task control and 32-byte
runtime continuation. The remaining task records and both command queues require
768 bytes. Packing the bounded tile index can physically fit those bytes in the
same existing union without consuming heap, but target timing remains decisive.

The first candidate packed all 1,808 bucket/chain indices into twelve bits,
saving 904 bytes. Representation/churn tests passed, but constructing 128 entries
per intro update failed the actor-state check at update 743. Constructing 32 per
update reached readiness at 784 and passed the intro; walking then failed at 966.
Candidate source, ROM, symbols and independent decoder are retained under
`build/packed-lookup12-candidate/`.

The second representation keeps 512 full-word heads and packs only 1,296 chain
links into eleven bits: 1,296 low bytes plus 244 aligned high-bit words (including
a guard word). Total lookup storage is 2,808 bytes instead of 3,616, saving 808.
Zero encodes an absent chain link, while heads retain ordinary FFFF sentinels.
Unlinked chain contents are unspecified and overwritten on reinsertion, removing
an unnecessary packed write. The candidate fits 512 task-record bytes and 256
queue bytes alongside the existing controls, leaving 44 bytes in the union.
These fields were only reserved, not initialized or scheduled.

The retained experimental `willow_native_tile_lookup_packed.h` and
`test-native-tile-lookup-packed` check all 1,297 valid link values at all 1,296
positions, neighboring packed fields, 262,144 churn operations, exhaustive ID
queries and collision-chain deletions with strict ASan/UBSan. This is representation
correctness, not production suitability (`build/packed-tile-lookup-host.log`).

The eleven-bit candidate passes the normal intro/walking-state probe and all
independent captured walking pixel comparisons (`build/packed-lookup-walk11.log`,
`build/packed-lookup-pixels.log`). However, the movement stress sequence beginning
input at 915 misses update 916. Keeping head sentinels unencoded, dropping the
unlinked-entry write and reducing native pin-release batches did not remove that
miss (`build/packed-lookup-stress{,-fast,-budget}.log`). The latest rejected source,
ROM, symbols and decoder are preserved in `build/packed-lookup11-candidate/`.
The pixel evidence belongs to the earlier eleven-bit build, not the final tuning
attempt. `tools/intro_rom_packed_lookup.c` is candidate-specific; it must not be
used to interpret the normal renderer's dense index.

Restored the validated main source and rebuilt it. The normal ROM is byte-identical
to the pre-experiment build, SHA256
`2501bf8b0d7cb4bcf7c218a557d0fe7b253dccd74bb29a5c49b348478266e9ea`.
The restored movement stress passes (`build/packed-lookup-restored-stress.log`).
No packed-index memory saving or task storage is counted in production capacity;
free heap stays 52 bytes. Task/global/palette memory and scheduler integration,
remaining gameplay, audio, campaign visuals and sustained 60 FPS remain unfinished.
All execution was headless.

### In-place post-intro ownership mirror: host representation proof (2026-10-04)

Added experimental `willow_native_tile_mirror.h`. It distinguishes the CPU
mirrors' two roles: dense intro words are complete VDP attributes and DMA
sources; post-publication ownership only needs each cell's eleven-bit VRAM tile
index. Two indices fit into three bytes, so 2,752 cells occupy 4,128 instead of
5,504 bytes, freeing 1,376 bytes once conversion is complete. This could fund
the 768 missing scheduler-record/queue bytes with 608 bytes left, without changing
the hot tile lookup. This is potential capacity, not a production allocation.

The helper converts forward in place with a bounded per-call budget. It reads
each dense word before overwriting its bytes; the compact prefix never touches
a later dense cell. A conversion cursor selects dense versus compact access,
allowing interleaved writes while preserving all attributes in cells that have
not converted. Compact cells intentionally retain ownership only; they cannot
be used as complete attribute/DMA sources. The integration must prove all old
DMA references retired, route each access correctly, and preserve full hardware
attributes from the original source. No production handoff is implemented yet.

`test-native-tile-mirror` passes strict warnings, ASan and fatal UBSan. It tests
all 2,048 tile values in each of 2,752 cells with unchanged neighbors, sixteen
complete conversions with interleaved writes and full dense-tail checks,
131,072 writes after conversion with the reclaimed tail overwritten as a guard,
and invalid bounds without mutation (`build/tile-mirror-host.log`). Native 68000
endianness, conversion cost, target frame timing, DMA lifetime and real rendered
pixels remain to be checked before integration. Host representation correctness
alone does not approve this layout.

The normal ROM and renderer source were not changed in this experiment; the
accepted task-control-bus build remains the production baseline. All work was
headless. Full gameplay/scheduler integration and the complete port remain open.

### Ownership mirror compiled 68000 representation and cost (2026-10-04)

Added `tools/tile_mirror_probe.c` and `test-native-tile-mirror-target`, compiling
the same experimental codec for the Genesis 68000. The independent host oracle
packs bits individually rather than invoking the codec. Across four complete
in-place conversions it interleaves writes and reads, checks every non-stack RAM
byte after each target call, verifies the full attributes of unconverted words,
and overwrites reclaimed storage with a guard during subsequent operations.
All 6,008 compiled calls match, including the big-endian in-place overlap cases
(`build/tile-mirror-target.log`). The harness runs the headless core CPU directly;
it calibrates its cycle-prefix access against a four-CPU-cycle NOP first.

The maximum measured conversion call with a budget of at most 65 cells costs
125,146 master cycles, about 14% of the 896,040-cycle NTSC frame budget. Maximum
write cost is 3,598 master cycles. These figures include the diagnostic command
wrapper and its loads/stores, not production frame costs. Conversion must be
spread across updates with verified spare time; neither these measurements nor
representation correctness prove that the real renderer can meet all deadlines.
Pending intro DMA ownership and full-attribute consumers must still be audited
and adapted before any dense data is converted or its tail reused.

Reproduce with `make test-native-tile-mirror-target SGDK_ROOT=/tmp/willow-sgdk-resume`.
The initial harness load failed because this core requires its ROM path to exist;
writing the private diagnostic file before loading fixed the harness setup.
The normal renderer and its validated ROM remain unchanged. No scheduler memory
saving is counted yet, and the port remains unfinished. All execution was headless.

### Resumable native ownership transpose with concurrent accesses (2026-10-04)

Added `willow_native_tile_mirror_transpose.h` to convert a fully compact
row-major ownership stream to the column-major layout required by the passing
steady-state renderer. It follows permutation cycles, retaining one displaced
tile between calls. Eight bytes of native progress state identify the scan,
cycle start, held tile's logical origin and value. A 344-byte visited bitmap
uses the start of the already-reclaimed tail. Each budget unit either skips
one completed location or advances one cycle edge; no unbounded scan occurs.
Logical reads/writes remain row-major while conversion proceeds and redirect to
the held value or its moved destination as appropriate. Scratch is not available
for task storage until this transpose finishes; the other 1,032 tail bytes are
not touched by the transpose. This is still a conversion component, not an
integrated handoff or task-memory allocation.

`test-native-tile-mirror-transpose` passes strict ASan/UBSan checks over sixteen
permutations: 7,812 batches, 21,498,624 logical-cell comparisons, 3,704 writes to
a live displaced tile, exact final layout, zero-budget calls, invalid-index
nonmutation and scratch/tail guards (`build/tile-mirror-transpose-host.log`).

Extended the compiled 68000 diagnostic with initialization, bounded steps,
logical reads and writes. An independent byte/bit oracle tracks source values
and permutation state; every non-stack RAM byte matches after all 2,944 new
calls, including 451 held-tile writes. All 6,008 previous compact conversion and
access cases also pass (`build/tile-mirror-transpose-target.log`). Compiling the
freestanding diagnostic explicitly prevents GCC introducing an unavailable
libc `memset`; normal ROM build flags are unchanged.

Maximum measured transpose call (budget <=41) is 255,038 master cycles, about

counted in production. All execution was headless. The port remains unfinished.

### Split full attributes: avoid the expensive ownership handoff conversion (2026-10-04)

Added experimental `willow_native_attribute_mirror.h` as an alternative to
converting and transposing the mirrors during play. It stores VDP attribute bits
0..11 in 4,128 packed bytes and bits 12..15 in a separate 1,376-byte nibble plane.
Together these occupy exactly the original 5,504 bytes and preserve EVERY 16-bit
attribute, not only observed forest palettes or flip combinations. It can be
column-major from the first write. Once full-attribute consumers retire, ownership
reads mask horizontal-flip bit 11 and ownership writes touch only the first
4,128 bytes, allowing the metadata tail to be reassigned without copying cells.
No blanket color conversion, restricted palette, or discarded live flip bit is
part of this representation.

attributes at both nibble parities, 131,072 interleaved full-attribute writes,

(`build/attribute-mirror-host.log`). Extended the compiled diagnostic with full
attribute and ownership operations: all 16,384 calls match every non-stack RAM
byte against an independent bit-level oracle, including calls after replacing
the complete metadata plane with a guard (`build/attribute-mirror-target.log`).
Earlier conversion and transpose tests also pass in the extended diagnostic.
Random traces differ after adding the attribute scenarios, so prior transpose
call counts/cycle maxima should not be compared as a code-speed measurement.

### Bulk plane retirement reduces active commit cost (2026-10-05)

Replaced per-cell free-slot maintenance in the guarded plane commit with
willowNativePlaneReleaseSpan followed by one availability rebuild. The span
helper retires only prevalidated owned cells, preserves attributes until the
bulk mirror clear, and leaves other owners' reference counts intact. Its 68000
path handles four cells per loop, biases the reference address register once,
and supports both contiguous offscreen rows and strided streamed columns.
The address bias stays inside assembly; C does not form an out-of-range pointer.
Zero-length and remainder spans are handled separately.

willowTileSlotsRebuild now builds one summary group at a time. The 68000 path
packs sixteen full-word reference predicates with NEG/ROXR, then inverts the

### Demo-state cold-start provenance (2026-10-05)

The original 05A6/05AA path invokes 06F2..0706 before entering normal startup.
That routine writes zero to the entire FF0000..FFFFFF work-RAM range, then
jumps through A4. Therefore the supplemental demo-state bytes, including the
828A saved pointer and F9A2 cycle, have zero cold-start values. Added a named
cold-reset projection in willow_native_demo_state.h; it is deliberately not a
demo-entry reset and is not yet called by cartridge startup.

Extended the headless original-instruction startup test with 32 cold-clear
cases. It checks all 65536 RAM bytes, terminal PC/A0/D0 and all 321 projected
bytes against the original CPU routine, in addition to the existing 8192
startup cases. ASan/UBSan run passes. Evidence: build/demo-cold-start-source.log.

This does not establish the values at demo entry. The existing source lifecycle
demo fixtures explicitly seed 828A with ROM pointer 183C; those fixtures cannot
prove that pointer's cold-start provenance. A subsequent integration must trace
the intervening services and preserve any writes. Also account for source ROM
address zero faithfully if the pointer remains zero: the CPU oracle currently
patches reset vectors for its Genesis harness. Do not mistake those harness
vector bytes for original arcade data. Demo dispatch remains disabled pending
that evidence and complete compiled initialization/resource checks.

### CPU cycle profiling and direct byte ownership (2026-10-05)

Added the optional host-only `WILLOW_PROFILE_DEMO_CYCLES=1` diagnostic in
`tools/native_cpu_cycles.h`. It measures the compiled 68000 service instructions
without advancing the other devices, then restores the save state and executes
the same call normally through `retro_run`. Every update requires identical
non-stack RAM below F600 and all 64 KiB SRAM between the two executions, as
well as the existing original-CPU-verified endpoint comparisons. No timing
instrumentation or extra working storage is added to the cartridge.

This uses Genesis Plus GX v1.7.4, commit `5a8389c`, installed-core SHA256
`88314cd8554a3cc5eebf00a4139e6f0dee9ea579dcb2321a0959579f1902fa09`.
The [core interface](https://github.com/ekeeke/Genesis-Plus-GX/blob/5a8389c/core/m68k/m68k.h)
defines `m68k_run` as running to an absolute clock target; `m68k_cycles()` is
only an opcode's base cost. The diagnostic reads the elapsed master counter,
validates the exposed prefix against all 16 CPU registers and PC, and checks
64 NOPs against 28 master ticks (or 42 with bus refresh). It also checks the
refresh field's update rule. The [save-state implementation](https://github.com/ekeeke/Genesis-Plus-GX/blob/5a8389c/core/state.c)
omits the refresh phase, so that one validated internal field is explicitly
restored alongside the normal save state and battery RAM. CPU registers and
the master counter must round-trip exactly. The injection's JSR and the service
return are counted; the terminal idle branch is never executed or counted.

`WILLOW_CYCLE_PROFILE_PREFIX` selects the output prefix (default
`build/demo-sequence`). The `-cycles.csv` file contains each update's cycles
and instruction count; `-cycle-pcs.csv` contains instruction-address totals.
Use `python3 tools/report_demo_cycles.py PREFIX EXACT_ROM_SYMBOLS` for function
attribution. The report checks that every measured instruction is in ROM,
apart from exactly one injected JSR per update. Two independent runs of the
previous fixed-table checkpoint produced byte-identical cycle CSVs and PC
tallies. Adding profiling also preserved its 1610/20 diagnostic slice result,
and the subsequent byte-adapter checkpoint's 1285/16 result.

| Guarded implementation | Total master cycles (120 updates) | Mean logic time | Peak logic time | Total/peak slices |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Previous fixed-owner table | 1387519994 | 215.347 ms | 317.480 ms | 1610 / 20 |
| Byte bus shortcut | 1090185950 | 169.200 ms | 266.726 ms | 1285 / 16 |
| Direct byte owner lookup | 1011350578 | 156.964 ms | 249.124 ms | 1179 / 15 |
| Direct lookup with ROM address bias | 1007839588 | 156.420 ms | 248.340 ms | 1178 / 15 |

The new byte reader, writer and fixed record resolution use the ownership
index directly for one-byte membership. Full-span access retains its bounds
checks. ROM metadata stores an unsigned 32-bit destination-minus-source bias,
so the mapper adds the source address after validating its owner. This stores
addresses only, never game state. An additional 65536 compiled pointer checks
compare the byte shortcut with the legacy resolver, alongside all 589824
address/span comparisons and the fixed/visibility non-overlap audit. The
existing host log intentionally reports only the common 589824 comparisons
because it also runs older retained ROMs without the extra checks.

The final guarded build retains all 120 matching endpoints and the continuous
3724-cycle / 8288-dispatch opening, uses no new working RAM and fits below
SRAM (`_stext = 0x1ffaa0`). The independent scene-spawn test also passes 512
actor updates, 5364 sprite pieces and 1572864 exact palette-word comparisons.
Evidence is in `build/demo-cycles-native-validated/`.
The new change reduces measured isolated CPU work by 7.55% from the byte-bus
checkpoint. Mean/peak time still exceeds a 60 Hz budget by 9.39x / 14.90x.
These are emulated CPU-only costs at the NTSC clock, not hardware measurements
or complete-game FPS: VDP/Z80/IRQ concurrency, active scheduler admission,
rendering/audio integration and full campaign coverage remain unfinished.

`port_save.h` explicitly serializes two128-byte journal slots per mode:512
logical SRAM bytes total. Each record carries magic/version/mode/payload length,
sequence, nine settings bytes, the independently maintained HUD best score,

exit, game start and post-name-entry/game-over return, not in every idle frame.

`port_save_sgdk.h` implements the standard odd-byte SRAM profile using the
pinned SRAM_* logical-offset API. It waits for active DMA, masks IRQs, holds
the Z80, enables SRAM, then disables SRAM/restores banks4/5 and prior bus ownership.
This is NOT an extended-SSF RAM-bank implementation or a physical flashcart
compatibility claim. The final linker must keep its full save call graph and
constants outside the overlaid ROM area, advertise SRAM200001..2003FF, and
reserve these bytes instead of enabling the old actor-SRAM probe. Hardware
power-cycle and complete cartridge save tests remain pending.

## Home New Game Plus — 2026-10-21

User-authorized Home customization, separate from the source arcade rules:
completing the ending on the initial credit unlocks NEW GAME PLUS beneath START
GAME. Lives and purchased extra lives remain within that credit. An admitted
Continue invalidates eligibility even in Home free play; ordinary game-over and
Arcade do not unlock it. The actual post-name-entry return checks the ending
latch and run eligibility. A fresh Home start clears the previous ending latch.

The unlock is monotonic during the session and is stored at payload byte 105 in
version 2 of the existing 512-byte SRAM journal (94-byte payload, same two 128-byte
slots per mode). Version 1 scores/settings migrate with NG+ locked. The new byte
is CRC-covered and range-checked; Arcade records cannot contain the Home unlock.
Save failures remain visible and leave the session unlock usable.

NG+ uses two energy points per source enemy-health unit. Fourteen packed bytes
across enemy, surface and boss pools retain the fractional energy; acquisition
clears the corresponding bit. This keeps one-HP enemies alive after the first
one-point hit and permits 360 effective energy for a 180-HP boss without overflowing
the original byte health or stretching its HUD. All shared damage policies,
piercing power consumption and blast thresholds use the effective energy.
Fractional hits invalidate the health-observation cache so native hit reactions
and recovery timers still run. Source scripted deaths/healing remain source
operations; fractional state persists through phases within the allocation.
Normal Home/Arcade targets use the original integer-health path.

All displayed and charged shop prices use the same 2x BCD conversion, capped at
the six-digit display maximum. Zero-cost items remain zero; the original price
escalation is retained unscaled and transformed at display/payment only, avoiding
compounding on shop re-entry. Starting an ordinary Home or Arcade run, and
returning to menus, disable NG+ combat/shop rules. Enemy counts are unchanged;
more enemies remain conditional on full-image fit and busy-scene headroom.

## Physical VBlank clock and boot audio binding — 2026-10-21

The production cartridge now contains `native/cartridge/clock.c`: a minimal
VINT counter ISR and a serialized foreground reader of VDP vertical position
and blanking status. The IRQ compiles to a counter increment followed by RTE;
it does not reenter game/audio work or touch the VDP command latch. Physical
boot installs this clock and the native FM/PSG/PCM output callbacks. Startup
must configure H40/V224 noninterlaced timing, configure the clock, enable VINT,
and observe the first interrupt before calling boot. This startup sequence and
physical display/controller main loop are still unbound.

The clock returns elapsed NTSC master-clock units, carrying the fractional PAL
conversion. It handles repeated vertical-counter values conservatively and
requires interrupts enabled during reads, no half-written VDP command, and no
whole-frame VINT masking. The documented sampling uncertainty is at most seven
NTSC or 58 PAL scanlines; this is not a promise of sub-scanline audio dispatch.
Its arithmetic checks exercise 69,870,888 samples, long intervals and counter
wraps. The production module also passes 1,200 normal-speed headless hardware
frames in each region, including soft reset and delayed foreground polling:
maximum frame-end errors were 23,940 NTSC and 20,709 PAL NTSC-clock units.
These are clock-module checks, not live campaign/audio or FPS acceptance.

Primary timing references consulted were Genesis Plus GX revision 5a8389c:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ekeeke/Genesis-Plus-GX/5a8389c/core/system.c,
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ekeeke/Genesis-Plus-GX/5a8389c/core/vdp_ctrl.c,
and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ekeeke/Genesis-Plus-GX/5a8389c/core/hvc.h.
The independently implemented clock treats the last overscan line's cleared
blanking flag and VINT's line-224 boundary explicitly. The production reader
waits past ambiguous raw VC224 with interrupts enabled between snapshots.

`cartridge-clock-v7` passes all eight steps; all ten recorded inputs were
independently rehashed unchanged after terminal completion. Earlier attempts
remain preserved. v5 exposed PAL sampling delay; v6 temporarily measured that
delay with a wider diagnostic bound. v7 avoids a second software division when
retaining the exact fractional remainder and restores the stricter 60,000-unit
headless frame-end bound. This is clock implementation work, not a reopening
of gameplay performance optimization.

`cartridge-platform-v16` compiles all six actual platform sources; 563 inputs
were rehashed unchanged. Boot's local stack frame rises from 360 to 768 bytes

acknowledgement, then hold reset before mapper/SRAM initialization. Cold and soft

## Physical controller binding and native startup timing — 2026-10-21

`native/cartridge/input.c` uses the pinned SGDK JOY initialization, detection,
selection and polling subsystem. Both direct three- and six-button pads feed the
existing button ABI. The target-only `willowCartridgeHardwareInterrupt` samples
both ports and calls the same Home/Arcade/credit/pause path as the connected
campaign. It is foreground dispatch, not an ISR. Target boot requires controller
initialization; after construction it samples current buttons and absorbs held
menu inputs before the first menu dispatch. The physical Main still must call
this at its serialized service boundary.

JOY's two masked startup VSync waits and three initial refresh waits bind to
real VDP-status waits, before clock/audio startup. Its ordinary port handshakes,
Z80 guards and pad decoding remain pinned SDK code. `build_sdk_controller.py`
collects the SDK functions with five explicit native bindings: those two startup
services plus register read/write/HV latch. `video_registers.c` is the native
register shadow shared by controller support and future video dispatch. It does
not import SGDK's unrelated DMA/fade/XGM task dispatcher or font/heap machinery.
No game tasks or audio jobs are due during these startup waits.

Cold input initialization obtains an acknowledged Z80 bus before JOY detection,
leaving Z80 parked for later audio-driver startup. Without this step, reset-held
Z80 looked unowned to the SDK IO guard and was released by that guard. This was
observed by input-check-v4, fixed in the production input owner, and validated
from v5 onward. Unsupported devices are disabled before the first JOY poll:
the pinned SDK Teamplayer reader otherwise calls a null event callback during
initialization. v1–v3 exposed this because the first harness selected a Teamplayer
preset by an overly broad description match. The corrected harness selects exact
advertised device descriptions. Failed versions and source backups are retained.

### Physical synchronous video transfer owner and dispatch boundaries

Added production `native/cartridge/video_transfer.[ch]` and included it in the real cartridge build. VRAM, CRAM and VSRAM writes synchronously consume aligned work-RAM words, accept sign-extended FFxxxx bus aliases, reject destination/source overrun and invalid CRAM values, account exact publication bytes, drain the hardware FIFO, and restore auto-increment/display state. No deferred stack buffer or DMA/main-bus ownership change is introduced. Begin requires live VINT epochs, H40/V224, display enabled and no HV latch. It admits only the early blank window; display is disabled during the granted blank interval to hide a fatal partial write. Successful writes restore it before active video. This guard is not a complete-publication WCET or admission proof; normal gameplay blank frames are not implemented or authorized by this change.

The target main dispatcher now checks transaction completion at task/IRQ boundaries. The exported target task wrapper checks before its post-task audio poll as well, because a disabled display alters status interpretation. Startup/input/save-audio boundaries also reject an open transfer. An incomplete or overrun transfer becomes a sticky fatal condition, with output hidden until reset. The newest test also rejects Begin with VINT masked.

### Live resource staging and upload consumption — 2026-10-22

`native/cartridge/video_stage.c` connects the physical-front helper to the
actual prepared background cache, sprite tuples and native allocation. It
resolves current cartridge resources into a bounded tile buffer and uploads
only destinations outside the captured front. It preserves pending counts,
front leases and published addresses. Before the first early write it dirties
unreferenced sprite cache entries; borrowed background slots are dirtied before
their pixels change. Cancelling a partial preparation therefore cannot expose
stale cached artwork on a subsequent acquire. A service callback may poll audio
between tiles, but must not advance source tasks or alter the frozen display.
Standalone text/sprite publication does not stage another owner's pending
background work.

The reservation bitmap occupies expired grouping workspace beside the physical
front. A guarded grant subtracts already-staged bytes from its physical budget;
this is accounting, **not timing admission**. The actual background/sprite upload
providers consume staged destinations through their ordinary callback path,
so cache retirement still happens at normal commit. The SAT provider verifies
that every staged destination has been consumed and releases the reservation
before rebuilding SAT in that same workspace. The only new persistent storage
is a four-byte target pointer. Refused grants invalidate the snapshot, and a
partial or inconsistent consumption cannot silently publish a new sprite list.
The missing platform binder still must prove/admit the remaining workload and
invoke this preparation; no always-success provider has been installed.

Incident: at 08:38 another local agent session deleted the whole `build/`
folder (and those of three other ports) to free disk space; it was restored
intact later the same morning. A log-based reconstruction was started and

were regenerated by the deterministic Makefile rule; the cartridge does not use them).

Implementation (all in `build/native-world/cartridge-output-binding-v1/candidate-v48`):
see RENDERER_REDESIGN.md "Implementation status". Native mode covers every scene
bound to the gameplay text overlay (campaign gameplay and its story scenes);
shop, frontend menus and the ending composite keep the retained renderer.
Additional changes made while measuring (each verified headlessly):
- Software physical front (no VRAM readback) in native mode: scenery slots
  leased at the last publication (front hint bit) + native front blocks +
  last published scroll; FrontSafe consults them per tile. The admission
  capture (FrontHints) is skipped in native mode. VRAM reads cost ~600 CPU
  cycles each under emulation; captures were ~24 frames each.
- Identical publications are skipped (exact copies of scroll, layer word,
  background colours; SAT/colour dirty flags).
- Palette projection is incremental: groups stay assigned; new pens/groups take
  exact or free page pens without moving existing ones; colour-only changes
  recolour in place; full pages approximate to the nearest page colour and a
  full rebuild (NN-based merge, epoch advance) runs at most ~once a second.
  Object pen usage is learned per group from pieces before composition.
- Bulk banked-ROM copies (`willowROMCopy`) for sprite tiles, row entries,
  palette groups, camera LZSS input (32-byte read-ahead) and background colours;
  window-7 mapping is kept lazily (no IRQ mask/restore per byte; window 7 is
  used only by foreground ROM readers). `check_cartridge_rom_access.c` still
  asserts the old mask/restore protocol and must be updated.
- Text layer: per-row dirty mask kept by the text surface; only dirty rows are
  rescanned (full scan on text scroll/layer/epoch change).
- Scenery plane-job queue: run-count delta computed locally (equivalent to the
  full per-row recount; 117,740 randomized checks); empty plans exit early.

## 2026-10-24: v49 compose kernel, timer calibration

- candidate-v48 source now builds link-v49 (5,238,096 bytes, link passed).
  Sprite block compose fuses pattern decode, pen remap and blit with byte
  shifts only (`willowSpritePatternPackMapped`/`RawMapped`); text glyph compose
  uses the same pixel expansion; the big-endian no-op word swap is compiled
  out on the 68000. Host check (scratchpad cmp_main.c, link-v47 data): all
  38,312 entry/flip compositions byte-identical to v48, including slots that
  map opaque pens to 0. Backups of the v48 headers are in the session scratchpad.
- Timer calibration (audio-frozen diag): an empty DSTART/DSTOP pair costs
  ~0.02 frame (~2.5k cycles); a 10,000-cycle dbra loop measures ~11.5k cycles,
  so the CPU is not starved; the code is simply slow (-Os register spills,
  32-bit arithmetic, per-byte banked ROM reads).
- Per source tick (2 commits, 1 begin/stage): commit 21.9 frames (prepare 5.6,
  begin 4.3, stage 5.2, upload 4.5, complete 1.3), game logic ~9.3 frames.
  The compose rewrite moved upload only ~0.1 frame: decode is ~12k cycles per
  tile and the remaining cost is spread across the inlined 2.8 KB `reserve`.
- Consequence: game logic alone (~9.3 frames/tick) caps the game at ~6 ticks/s
  even with free rendering. The original arcade program runs the same logic on
  a 10 MHz 68000 inside one frame, so the translated engine is ~7x slower than
  the source code it reproduces. 45 FPS needs that gap closed as well as the
  PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md rendering and audio rewrites.

## 2026-10-24: projection and scenery-lookup findings (no code change kept)

- Palette projection rebuilds are rare (2 per 61 ticks, 3 approximate
  extends); each rebuild is ~15k colour distances. A symmetric first pass
  would halve that but needs a 256-byte stack array for ~0.5% of frame time,
  so it was reverted.
- `willowPatternFind` (5.7% self time) is a full scan: the background cache
  has WILLOW_GAME_BACKGROUND_BUCKETS=1 and cursor allocation, so every lookup
  walks up to 1,360 three-byte slots. Keys are unique (install only after a
  failed find), so an exact hash index would return the same slot. No
  persistent RAM exists for one (12 bytes free); the 2,560-byte grouping
  workspace is reused by the front/stage reservation every publication, and
  rebuilding a 2 KB index per pass costs ~1 frame against ~1.7 saved.
  A persistent index needs RAM freed from the retained (non-native) renderer.

  Self-time leaders: MusicTick 7.0 (largely the eight-track quiet-countdown
  loop, ~150 cycles per track per tick), AdvanceTo 2.6, data reads 2.5, YM
  path 1.7, register mapping 1.5. Ports and data reads are already inlined /
  hinted; no single routine offers more than ~4%. Bulk-advancing all-quiet
  ticks or moving the sequencer to the Z80 are the remaining levers.
- Sampling caveat: PCSAMPLE=2 samples at frame end, and the source latch
  (willowCartridgeVideoLatch -> SceneScroll -> unchanged commit) runs at a
  fixed point after VBlank, so latch-time code is over-represented. Example:
  BackgroundColorsReady shows 3.8% under the latch path although it is a
  30-entry validation loop; the counter build measures the whole unchanged
  commit at ~1.1 frames per tick. Treat fp shares of latch-time code as upper
  bounds; cross-check with counters_rel.sh.

## 2026-10-24: v52 persistent scenery key index

  gameplay is active. WillowPatternCache gains an optional `index` pointer;
  the exact key index (2,048 one-byte entries holding slot%254+1, linear
  probing, verified against stored key bytes, insert-only with rebuild at
  1,640 entries or after any lookup reset) lives in the retained renderer's
  sprite tuple arena (`keys` 2,048 bytes + header in `entries`). Native
  entry empties that unreferenced tuple cache; leaving restores an empty,
  consistent arena. Installed keys are unique, so the indexed slot equals the
  scan's slot: host check 1,504,051 lookups identical under random
  acquire/release/invalidate/relink traffic.
- link-v52: 5,240,506 bytes, BSS end 0xfff2fc (4 bytes free). Home run: no
  fault, PLAY at frame 95,551 (v51 97,918), 29.7 frames per source tick
  (v51 30.6). Control captures (idle/right/jump/attack/finished) are
  byte-identical to v51. Profile: willowPatternFind 5.8% -> 0.4%; scenery
  stream 10.7% -> 5.7%.

  (game logic, latch/IRQ, emission) is ~5-6 frames, and real 68000 audio adds
  ~6-7 (audio-on counter builds inflate audio, since every SaveAudio call
  reads the clock twice; use the uninstrumented ~29 vs audio-frozen ~23
  frames/tick difference). Publishing one tick in n gives roughly
  12 + 17/n frames per tick: n=2 -> ~20 (3 ticks/s), n=4 -> ~16 (3.7 ticks/s).

## 2026-10-24: v55 audio/logic pass (user: "do audio and logic first")

- Audio: the music tick's leading quiet-countdown tracks now run with
  hoisted loop invariants (global[0x14]&1 and the fade-hold test), falling
  back to the original per-track routine at the first non-quiet track.
  Audio golden unchanged on fast and reference port builds (833,370 ticks,
  output 229c9b5d, state 578c143a; ASan/UBSan clean).
- Logic: willowWorldDictionaryCell (player wall contacts) uses one 16/32-bit
  ROM read per value instead of 2/4 byte calls; admission already proves the
  offsets even, so values are identical.
- link-v55: 5,240,506 bytes, no fault, control captures identical to v54,
  tick_fit 28.3 frames/tick (v54 28.2): below measurement resolution.
- Findings: audio (~24% of real time) has no cheap lever: per-write Z80 bus
  locking protects PCM4, pre-rendered streams cannot fit in ~2.3 KB of ROM,
  and the sequencer's cost is spread over step/note/levels/chip writes.
  Logic (~25% of audio-free time) is spread across player contacts (~5%),
  entity/surface scans (~10%; 48-slot jump-table scans run several times per
  tick) and sprite template emission (~6%). Larger gains need structural
  changes: active-slot lists maintained at every activation site, a Z80
  music driver (with a PCM mixing tradeoff), or ROM space for -O2 hot paths.
- Correction: a counter build shows willowNativeSurfaceScan runs once per
  source tick (81 scans / 81 loops). Its inactive-slot skipping is ~6k cycles
  (~0.05 frame); the sampled self time is the inlined platform step bodies.
  Active-slot lists would therefore save almost nothing; withdrawn.
- Same counter run: audio-frozen v55 averages 24.7 frames per loop (v48
  instrumented: ~35).

## 2026-10-24: Z80 budget for a combined music+PCM driver

- SGDK PCM4 (drv_pcm4.s80): 223 Z80 cycles per output sample at a fixed
  16 kHz = ~3.57M cycles/s, i.e. the whole 3.58 MHz Z80. No room exists for
  the music sequencer beside it.
- The source samples are OKI MSM6295 voices at 1 MHz/132 = ~7,575.76 Hz
  (four voices). The cartridge stores them upsampled to 16 kHz 8-bit PCM
  (0x200000..0x2f9b00, ~1,022 KB).
- A combined driver mixing the four voices at the native ~7.58 kHz needs
  ~223*7,576 = ~1.69M cycles/s (47% of the Z80), leaving ~1.9M cycles/s, about
  7.9k Z80 cycles per 240 Hz music tick, for the translated sequencer and the
  YM2151->YM2612/PSG mapping (68000 today: ~5.5k cycles per tick). Storing
  the clips at the native rate would also free roughly 540 KB of ROM, enough
  to compile hot engine paths for speed. Not implemented: needs user approval
  (sound pipeline change) and a Z80 cycle proof of the sequencer per tick.
- User approved (2026-10-24) the combined Z80 driver: four OKI voices mixed
  at the native ~7.58 kHz plus the music sequencer, verified against the
  audio golden and cue timing.
- Sequencer work per 249.7 Hz source tick (host golden run, 833,370 ticks):
  1.8 data reads and 1.56 chip writes on average; 96.2% of ticks are
  countdown-only; peaks reach 362 reads / 353 writes (song/patch loads),
  which must be absorbed over several ticks with elapsed-tick catch-up, as
  the source Z80 also could not finish them inside one timer period.
  Average Z80 cost is estimated at ~1-1.5k cycles per tick against the
  ~7.9k left after native-rate mixing.
